title.zh: 卷一百四十五 列傳第七十 元王黎楊嚴竇
title.en: Volume 145 Biographies 70: Yuan, Wang, Li, Yang, Yan, Dou
title.raw: 卷一百四十五 列傳第七十 元王黎楊嚴竇 Volume 145 Biographies 70: Yuan, Wang, Li, Yang, Yan, Dou

sentences.zh: 元王黎楊嚴竇

translations.literal: Yuan, Wang, Li, Yang, Yan, Dou
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Yuan Zai, Wang Jin, Li Gan, Yang Yan, and Dou Huaizhen

sentences.zh: 元載，字公輔，鳳翔岐山人。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai, styled Gongfu, was a native of Qishan in Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai, courtesy name Gongfu, came from Qishan in Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 父昇，本景氏。

translations.literal: His father Sheng was originally of the Jing clan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng was originally surnamed Jing.

sentences.zh: 曹王明妃元氏賜田在扶風，昇主其租入，有勞，請於妃，冒為元氏。

translations.literal: The honored consort of Lord Cao Ming, surnamed Yuan, had granted fields in Fufeng; Sheng managed their rent, and for his service requested of the consort to falsely claim the surname Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The honored consort of Prince Cao Ming of the Yuan clan held granted estates in Fufeng. Sheng managed the rental income and, for his labors, petitioned the consort to let him falsely adopt the surname Yuan.

sentences.zh: 載少孤，既長，嗜學，工屬文。

translations.literal: Zai was orphaned young; when grown, he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zai lost his father early. As he grew up, he became devoted to learning and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，下詔舉明莊、老、列、文四子學者，載策入高第，補新平尉。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era, an edict was issued to promote scholars versed in Zhuangzi, Laozi, Liezi, and Wenzi; Zai's examination essay ranked highest and he was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao reign, the court issued an edict summoning scholars proficient in the Four Masters—Zhuangzi, Laozi, Liezi, and Wenzi. Zai's examination essay placed in the top tier, and he was appointed assistant magistrate of Xinping.

sentences.zh: 韋鎰監選黔中，苗晉卿東都留守，皆署判官，浸以名聞。

translations.literal: When Wei Yi supervised selections in Qianzhong and Miao Jinqing served as Eastern Capital governor, both appointed him as administrative aide, and gradually his name became known.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Yi supervised civil examinations in Qianzhong and Miao Jinqing served as governor of the Eastern Capital, both men appointed him as an administrative aide. His reputation gradually spread.

sentences.zh: 至德初，江都采訪使李希言表載自副，擢祠部員外郎、洪州刺史。

translations.literal: In the early Zhide era, Jiangdu Regional Inspector Li Xiyang recommended Zai as his deputy, and he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhide reign, Li Xiyang, regional inspector of Jiangdu, recommended Zai as his deputy. Zai was then promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Rites and appointed prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為度支郎中，占奏敏給，肅宗異之。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of Revenue in the Ministry of Revenue; his memorials were swift and responsive, and Emperor Suzong found him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the capital as director of revenue in the Ministry of Revenue, his memorials were sharp and prompt, and Emperor Suzong took notice of him.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部侍郎，充度支、江淮轉運等使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and served concurrently as Commissioner of Revenue and of Huai–Jiang River transport.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to vice minister of revenue and concurrently served as commissioner of revenue and of Huai–Jiang transport.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，李輔國用事，輔國妻，載宗女也，因相締昵。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was unwell, Li Fuguo wielded power; Fuguo's wife was Zai's clanswoman by marriage, and thus they became closely allied.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, Li Fuguo dominated the court. Fuguo's wife was a kinswoman of Zai's clan, and the two men formed a close alliance.

sentences.zh: 會京兆尹缺，輔國白用載，載意屬國柄，固辭，輔國曉之，翌日，拜同中書門下平章事，領使如故。

translations.literal: When the office of Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao fell vacant, Fuguo recommended Zai for the post; Zai's intention was the chief minister's power, so he firmly declined; Fuguo made him understand, and the next day he was appointed Co-Signatory Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat, continuing his commissioner duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of metropolitan governor of Jingzhao fell vacant, Fuguo recommended Zai. Zai wanted actual control of state affairs rather than a local post and firmly declined. After Fuguo persuaded him, the next day Zai was appointed co-signatory director of the Chancellery and Secretariat while retaining his previous commissioner posts.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，輔國勢愈重，數稱其才，進拜中書侍郎、許昌縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Fuguo's power grew ever greater; he repeatedly praised Zai's talent, and Zai was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and made Viscount of Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Daizong took the throne, Fuguo's power grew even greater. He repeatedly praised Zai's talent, and Zai was promoted to vice director of the Chancellery and ennobled as Viscount of Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 載以度支繁浩，有吏事督責，損威寵，乃悉天下錢谷委劉晏。

translations.literal: Zai considered the revenue administration too complex, with clerical duties and supervision that diminished his prestige and favor, and therefore entrusted all the empire's finances and grain to Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zai found the revenue administration too burdensome—its clerical duties and supervisory obligations eroded his prestige and favor—so he entrusted all imperial finances and grain supply to Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，判天下元帥行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Before long, he was appointed Acting Chief of Staff to the Commander-in-Chief of the Empire.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was appointed acting chief of staff to the commander-in-chief of the empire.

sentences.zh: 盜殺李輔國，載陰與其謀。

translations.literal: Robbers killed Li Fuguo, and Zai had secretly plotted with them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo was killed by assassins, and Zai had secretly conspired in the plot.

sentences.zh: 乃復結中人董秀，厚啖以金，使刺取密旨，帝有所屬，必先知之，探微揣端，無不諧契，故帝任不疑。

translations.literal: He then again allied with the eunuch Dong Xiu, bribing him heavily with gold to spy out secret imperial intentions; whenever the Emperor had someone in mind for appointment, Zai always knew beforehand; probing subtleties and gauging implications, nothing failed to accord, and therefore the Emperor entrusted him without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He then allied himself with the eunuch Dong Xiu, bribing him heavily with gold to learn the emperor's secret intentions. Whenever the emperor had someone in mind for appointment, Zai always knew beforehand. Probing subtleties and gauging implications, he never missed the mark, and the emperor entrusted him without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 華原令顧繇上封白髮其私，帝方倚以當國，乃斥繇，除名為民。

translations.literal: Gu Yao, magistrate of Huayuan, submitted a sealed memorial exposing Zai's private misconduct; the Emperor was then relying on Zai to govern the state, and therefore dismissed Yao, stripping him of office and making him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yao, magistrate of Huayuan, submitted a sealed memorial exposing Zai's private misconduct. The emperor was then relying on Zai to govern the state, so he dismissed Yao, stripped him of office, and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩驕橫震天下，與載不葉，憚之，雖帝亦銜恚，乃乘間奏誅朝恩，帝畏有變，載結其愛將為助。

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en was arrogant and overbearing, shaking the empire; he and Zai were incompatible, and Zai feared him; though the Emperor also harbored resentment, Zai seized an opportunity to memorialize for Chao'en's execution; the Emperor feared trouble, and Zai enlisted his favorite generals as allies.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en was arrogant and overbearing, and his power shook the empire. He and Zai were at odds, and Zai feared him. Though the emperor also nursed resentment, Zai seized an opportunity to memorialize for Chao'en's execution. The emperor feared unrest, and Zai enlisted his favorite generals as allies.

sentences.zh: 朝恩已誅，載得意甚，益矜肆。

translations.literal: Once Chao'en was executed, Zai was greatly pleased and became even more arrogant and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chao'en was executed, Zai was greatly pleased and became even more arrogant and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 時擬奏文武官功狀多謬舛，載虞有司駁正，乃請別敕授六品以下官，吏部、兵部即附甲團奏，不須檢勘，欲示權出於己。

translations.literal: At the time, proposed memorials on the merits of civil and military officials often contained errors; Zai feared that the responsible offices would reject and correct them, and therefore requested that appointments below the sixth rank be granted by separate edict, with the Ministries of Personnel and War simply attaching lists and submitting jointly without review, wishing to show that power issued from himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, proposed memorials on the merits of civil and military officials often contained errors. Zai feared that the responsible offices would reject and correct them, so he requested that appointments below the sixth rank be granted by separate edict, with the Ministries of Personnel and War simply attaching lists and submitting jointly without review—seeking to show that power issued from himself alone.

sentences.zh: 又與王縉請以河中為中都，裒關輔河東十州稅奉京師，選兵五萬屯中都，鎮禦四方，杪秋行幸，上春還，可以避羌戎患。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Jin, he also requested that Hezhong be made the Central Capital, gathering taxes from ten prefectures of Guanfu and Hedong to supply the capital, selecting fifty thousand troops to garrison the Central Capital and guard all directions, with the Emperor traveling there in late autumn and returning in early spring, so as to avoid the menace of the Qiang and Rong barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Wang Jin, he also proposed making Hezhong the Central Capital, gathering taxes from ten prefectures in Guanfu and Hedong to supply the capital, selecting fifty thousand troops to garrison the Central Capital and guard all directions, with the emperor traveling there in late autumn and returning in early spring so as to avoid the menace of the Qiang and Rong barbarians.

sentences.zh: 載以議入，即從，前敕所由吏於河中經圖宮殿，築私第。

translations.literal: Zai submitted the proposal and it was immediately accepted; clerks who had previously carried out imperial edicts surveyed palace sites at Hezhong and built private mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Zai submitted the proposal and it was immediately accepted. Clerks who had previously carried out imperial edicts surveyed palace sites at Hezhong and built private mansions.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，惡之，置其議。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, he was disgusted and set the proposal aside.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he was disgusted and set the proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 初，四鎮北庭行營節度使寄治涇州，大歷八年，吐蕃寇邠寧，議者謂三輔以西無襟帶之固，而涇州散地不足守。

translations.literal: Initially, the Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and Beiting Field Headquarters had his seat at Jingzhou; in the eighth year of the Dali era, the Tibetans raided Binning; commentators said that west of the Three Metropolises there was no secure strategic belt, and that Jingzhou's scattered territory was insufficient to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, the military commissioner of the Four Garrisons and Beiting Field Headquarters had his seat at Jingzhou. In the eighth year of the Dali era, the Tibetans raided Binning. Commentators argued that west of the Three Metropolises there was no secure strategic belt, and that Jingzhou's scattered territory was insufficient to defend.

sentences.zh: 載嘗在西州，具知河西、隴右要領，乃言於帝曰：「國家西境極於潘原，吐蕃防戍乃在摧沙堡，而原州界其間，草薦水甘，舊壘存焉，比吐蕃毀夷垣墉，棄不居，其右則監牧故地，巨塹長壕，重復深固。

translations.literal: Zai had once served in Xizhou and thoroughly understood the strategic essentials of Hexi and Longyou; he said to the Emperor: "The state's western border extends to Panyuan; the Tibetan garrison is at Cuisha Fort, and Yuanzhou lies between them; the grass is fine and the water sweet, and old ramparts still stand there; recently the Tibetans destroyed and leveled the walls and abandoned the place; to its east lies the former pasture-administration land, with great moats and long trenches—layer upon layer of deep fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Zai had once served in Xizhou and thoroughly understood the strategic essentials of Hexi and Longyou. He said to the emperor: "The state's western border extends to Panyuan. The Tibetan garrison is at Cuisha Fort, and Yuanzhou lies between them. The grass is fine and the water sweet, and old ramparts still stand there. Recently the Tibetans destroyed and leveled the walls and abandoned the place. To its east lies the former pasture-administration land, with great moats and long trenches—layer upon layer of deep fortifications.

sentences.zh: 原州雖早霜不可蓺，而平涼在其東，獨耕一縣，可以足食。

translations.literal: Although Yuanzhou suffers early frosts and cannot be planted, Pingliang lies to its east; farming that one county alone can provide sufficient food.
translations.idiomatic: Although Yuanzhou suffers early frosts and cannot be planted, Pingliang lies to its east; farming that one county alone can provide sufficient food.

sentences.zh: 請徙京西軍戍原州，乘間築作，二旬可訖，貯粟一歲。

translations.literal: I request moving the Jingxi army to garrison Yuanzhou, seizing the opportunity to build fortifications—this can be completed in twenty days, with a year's grain stored.
translations.idiomatic: I request moving the Jingxi army to garrison Yuanzhou, seizing the opportunity to build fortifications—this can be completed in twenty days, with a year's grain stored.

sentences.zh: 戎人夏牧青海上，羽書比至，則我功集矣。

translations.literal: When the barbarians pasture on Qinghai in summer, urgent dispatches will arrive in succession, and by then our work will be complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians pasture on Qinghai in summer, urgent dispatches will arrive in succession, and by then our work will be complete.

sentences.zh: 徙子儀大軍在涇，以為根本，分兵守石門、木峽，隴山之關，北抵於河，皆連山峻險，寇不可越。

translations.literal: Move Guo Ziyi's main army to Jingzhou as the base, deploy troops to hold Shimen and Muxia, the passes of Longshan, north to the Yellow River—all connected mountain ridges, steep and perilous, that invaders cannot cross.
translations.idiomatic: Move Guo Ziyi's main army to Jingzhou as the base, deploy troops to hold Shimen and Muxia, the passes of Longshan, north to the Yellow River—all connected mountain ridges, steep and perilous, that invaders cannot cross.

sentences.zh: 稍置鳴沙縣、豐安軍為之羽翼，北帶靈武五城，為之形勢，然後舉隴右之地，以至安西，是謂斷西戎脛，朝廷高枕矣。」

translations.literal: Gradually establish Mingxia County and Feng'an Army as supporting wings; to the north link the five cities of Lingwu to create strategic posture; then recover the lands of Longyou all the way to Anxi—this is what is meant by severing the shins of the Western barbarians, and the court can rest on its pillows in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually establish Mingxia County and Feng'an Army as supporting wings; to the north link the five cities of Lingwu to create strategic posture; then recover the lands of Longyou all the way to Anxi—this is what is meant by severing the shins of the Western barbarians, and the court can rest on its pillows in peace.

sentences.zh: 因圖上地形，使吏間入原州度水泉，計徒庸，車乘畚鍤之器悉具。

translations.literal: He then submitted a map of the terrain and sent officials secretly into Yuanzhou to survey water sources, calculated labor requirements, and prepared carts, baskets, and shovels in full.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a map of the terrain and sent officials secretly into Yuanzhou to survey water sources, calculated labor requirements, and prepared carts, baskets, and shovels in full.

sentences.zh: 而田神功沮短其議，乃曰：「興師料敵，老將所難，陛下信一書生言，舉國從之，誤矣。」

translations.literal: But Tian Shen'gong disparaged the proposal and said: "Mobilizing troops and estimating the enemy is what even veteran generals find difficult; Your Majesty trusts the words of one scholar and would have the whole state follow him—this is a mistake.
translations.idiomatic: But Tian Shen'gong disparaged the proposal and said: "Mobilizing troops and estimating the enemy is what even veteran generals find difficult. Your Majesty trusts the words of one scholar and would have the whole state follow him—this is a mistake.

sentences.zh: 帝由是疑不決。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore became doubtful and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore became doubtful and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 載智略開果，久得君，以為文武才略莫己若。

translations.literal: Zai was resourceful, open, and decisive; having long enjoyed the Emperor's trust, he considered that in talent and strategy, civil and military, none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was resourceful, open, and decisive. Having long enjoyed the emperor's trust, he considered that in talent and strategy, civil and military, none could match him.

sentences.zh: 外委主書卓英倩、李待榮，內劫婦言，縱諸子關通貨賄。

translations.literal: Outwardly he entrusted affairs to chief clerks Zhuo Yingqian and Li Dairong; inwardly he relied on his wife's words and allowed his sons to traffic in bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he entrusted affairs to chief clerks Zhuo Yingqian and Li Dairong; inwardly he relied on his wife's influence and allowed his sons to traffic in bribes.

sentences.zh: 京師要司及方面，皆擠遣忠良，進貪猥。

translations.literal: In the capital's key offices and in the regions, he always squeezed out the loyal and good and advanced the greedy and base.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital's key offices and in the regions, he always squeezed out the loyal and good and advanced the greedy and base.

sentences.zh: 凡仕進幹請，不結子弟，則謁主書。

translations.literal: For all advancement and petitions for office, if one did not cultivate his sons, one had to visit the chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: For all advancement and petitions for office, if one did not cultivate his sons, one had to visit the chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 城中開南北二第，室宇奢廣，當時為冠。

translations.literal: In the city he opened two mansions, north and south; the buildings were luxurious and vast, unmatched at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the city he maintained two mansions, north and south; the buildings were luxurious and vast, unmatched at the time.

sentences.zh: 近郊作觀榭，帳帟什器不徙而供。

translations.literal: In the nearby suburbs he built pavilions and terraces; tents, curtains, and utensils were supplied without being moved.
translations.idiomatic: In the nearby suburbs he built pavilions and terraces; tents, curtains, and utensils were supplied without being moved from place to place.

sentences.zh: 膏腴別墅，疆畛相望，且數十區。

translations.literal: Fertile villa estates, their boundaries stretching one after another, numbered several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: He owned several dozen fertile villa estates, their boundaries stretching one after another across the countryside.

sentences.zh: 名姝異伎，雖禁中不逮。

translations.literal: Renowned beauties and exotic performers—even the inner palace could not match them.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned beauties and exotic performers—even the inner palace could not match them.

sentences.zh: 帝盡得其狀。

translations.literal: The Emperor learned the full extent of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned the full extent of it.

sentences.zh: 載嘗獨見，帝深戒之，謷然不悛。

translations.literal: Zai was once received in private audience; the Emperor sternly admonished him, but he remained arrogant and unrepentant.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was once received in private audience; the emperor sternly admonished him, but he remained arrogant and unrepentant.

sentences.zh: 客有賦《都盧尋橦篇》諷其危，載泣下而不知悟。

translations.literal: A guest composed the "Dulu Pole-Climbing Ballad" to satirize his peril; Zai wept but did not understand and repent.
translations.idiomatic: A guest composed the "Dulu Pole-Climbing Ballad" to satirize his peril; Zai wept but did not understand and repent.

sentences.zh: 會李少良上書詆其醜狀，載怒，奏殺少良，道路目語，不敢復議。

translations.literal: When Li Shaoliang submitted a memorial denouncing his ugly conduct, Zai was enraged and memorialized for Shaoliang's execution; people on the roads exchanged glances and dared not discuss it again.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shaoliang submitted a memorial denouncing his ugly conduct, Zai was enraged and memorialized for Shaoliang's execution. People on the roads exchanged glances and dared not discuss it again.

sentences.zh: 載由是非黨與不復接，生平道義交皆謝絕。

translations.literal: From then on Zai no longer received anyone who was not of his faction, and cut off all his lifelong friends bound by principle and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Zai no longer received anyone who was not of his faction, and cut off all his lifelong friends bound by principle and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 帝積怒，大歷十二年三月庚辰，仗下，帝禦延英殿，遣左金吾大將軍吳湊收載及王縉，系政事堂，分捕親吏、諸子下獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor's accumulated anger burst forth; on the gengchen day of the third month of the twelfth year of Dali, after the court session, the Emperor attended the Yanying Hall and dispatched Left General of the Imperial Guard Wu Cou to arrest Zai and Wang Jin, binding them in the Hall of Administration; he separately sent officers to capture Zai's personal clerks and sons and imprison them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's accumulated anger burst forth. On the gengchen day of the third month of the twelfth year of Dali, after the court session, the emperor attended the Yanying Hall and dispatched Left General of the Imperial Guard Wu Cou to arrest Zai and Wang Jin, binding them in the Hall of Administration. He separately sent officers to capture Zai's personal clerks and sons and imprison them.

sentences.zh: 詔吏部尚書劉晏、御史大夫李涵、散騎常侍蕭昕、兵部侍郎袁、禮部侍郎常袞、諫議大夫杜亞訊狀，而責辨端目皆出禁中。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Personnel Liu Yan, Censor-in-Chief Li Han, Palace Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Cong, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gun, and Remonstrance Officer Du Ya to investigate the case, but the charges and points of inquiry all issued from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Minister of Personnel Liu Yan, Censor-in-Chief Li Han, Palace Attendant Xiao Xin, Vice Minister of War Yuan Cong, Vice Minister of Rites Chang Gun, and Remonstrance Officer Du Ya to investigate the case, but the charges and points of inquiry all issued from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 遣中使臨詰陰事，皆服。

translations.literal: Palace envoys were dispatched to question them on secret matters, and all confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys were dispatched to question them on secret matters, and all confessed.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔賜載自盡，妻王及子揚州兵曹參軍伯和、祠部員外郎仲武、校書郎季能並賜死，發其祖、父冢，斫棺棄屍，毀私廟主及大寧、安仁裏二第，以賜百官署舍，披東都第助治禁苑。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued granting Zai death by his own hand; his wife Wang and his sons Bohe, Military Staff Officer of Yangzhou, Zhongwu, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and Jineng, Collator, were all granted death; their ancestral and paternal tombs were opened, coffins hacked open and corpses discarded; private ancestral tablets and the two mansions in Daning and Anren wards were destroyed and granted as office quarters for officials; the Eastern Capital mansion was demolished to help expand the Imperial Park.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued granting Zai death by his own hand. His wife Wang and his sons Bohe, military staff officer of Yangzhou, Zhongwu, vice director in the Ministry of Rites, and Jineng, collator, were all granted death. Their ancestral and paternal tombs were opened, coffins hacked open and corpses discarded. Private ancestral tablets and the two mansions in Daning and Anren wards were destroyed and granted as office quarters for officials. The Eastern Capital mansion was demolished to help expand the Imperial Park.

sentences.zh: 王氏，河西節度使忠嗣女，悍驕戾沓，載叵禁。

translations.literal: Lady Wang, daughter of Military Commissioner of Hexi Wang Zhongsi, was fierce, arrogant, perverse, and unrestrained; Zai could not restrain her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang, daughter of Military Commissioner of Hexi Wang Zhongsi, was fierce, arrogant, perverse, and unrestrained; Zai could not restrain her.

sentences.zh: 而諸子牟賊，聚斂無涯藝，輕浮者奔走。

translations.literal: His sons were greedy and violent, amassing wealth without limit; the frivolous rushed to their service.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were greedy and violent, amassing wealth without limit; the frivolous rushed to their service.

sentences.zh: 爭蓄妓妾，為倡優褻戲，親族環觀不愧也。

translations.literal: They vied to keep courtesans and concubines, performing lewd entertainments with actors and singers while kinsmen looked on in a circle without shame.
translations.idiomatic: They vied to keep courtesans and concubines, performing lewd entertainments with actors and singers while kinsmen looked on in a circle without shame.

sentences.zh: 及死，行路無嗟隱者。

translations.literal: When he died, no one on the road sighed or mourned in private.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, no one on the road sighed or mourned in private.

sentences.zh: 籍其家，鐘乳五百兩，詔分賜中書、門下臺省官，胡椒至八百石，它物稱是。

translations.literal: When his household goods were inventoried, there were five hundred liang of stalactite; an edict ordered it divided and granted to officials of the Chancellery, Secretariat, and central ministries; pepper reached eight hundred shi, and other goods were proportionate.
translations.idiomatic: When his household goods were inventoried, there were five hundred liang of stalactite; an edict ordered it divided and granted to officials of the Chancellery, Secretariat, and central ministries. Pepper reached eight hundred shi, and other goods were proportionate.

sentences.zh: 女真一，少為尼，沒入掖庭。

translations.literal: His daughter Zhenyi, who had become a nun in youth, was taken into the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Zhenyi, who had become a nun in youth, was taken into the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 德宗時，始告以載死，號踴投地，左右呵止，帝曰：「安有聞親喪責其哀殞乎？」

translations.literal: In Emperor Dezong's time, she was finally told of Zai's death; she wailed and threw herself to the ground; attendants shouted at her to stop; the Emperor said: "How can one, upon hearing of a parent's death, reproach her for grieving to the point of collapse?
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Dezong's time, she was finally told of Zai's death. She wailed and threw herself to the ground. Attendants shouted at her to stop. The emperor said: "How can one, upon hearing of a parent's death, reproach her for grieving to the point of collapse?

sentences.zh: 命扶出。

translations.literal: He ordered her assisted out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered her assisted out.

sentences.zh: 英倩弟英璘，家金州，州人緣以授官者亦百餘，豪制鄉曲，聚無賴少年以伺變，恃載權，牧宰莫敢問。

translations.literal: Yingqian's younger brother Yinglin lived in Jin Prefecture; more than a hundred local men had obtained office through his connections; he tyrannized the countryside, gathered idle youths to watch for opportunities, and relied on Zai's power, so prefects and magistrates dared not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqian's younger brother Yinglin lived in Jin Prefecture. More than a hundred local men had obtained office through his connections. He tyrannized the countryside, gathered idle youths to watch for opportunities, and relied on Zai's power, so prefects and magistrates dared not inquire.

sentences.zh: 載誅，英璘盜庫兵據險以叛。

translations.literal: When Zai was executed, Yinglin stole arsenal weapons, seized strategic terrain, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai was executed, Yinglin stole arsenal weapons, seized strategic terrain, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 詔發禁兵及山南西道兵二千討捕，刺史孫道平禽殺之。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched imperial guard troops and two thousand soldiers of Shannan West Circuit to pursue and capture him; Prefect Sun Daoping seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched imperial guard troops and two thousand soldiers of Shannan West Circuit to pursue and capture him. Prefect Sun Daoping seized and killed him.

sentences.zh: 詔給復其州三年。

translations.literal: An edict granted the prefecture tax relief for three years.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the prefecture tax relief for three years.

sentences.zh: 李少良者，以吏治由諸帥府遷累殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Li Shaoliang, through administrative competence, rose from various commanders' staffs by successive promotion to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaoliang, through administrative competence, rose from various commanders' staffs by successive promotion to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 罷，遊京師，不見調，憤載不法，疏論其惡，帝留少良客省，欲究其事。

translations.literal: When dismissed, he traveled to the capital but received no appointment; indignant at Zai's lawlessness, he submitted a memorial discussing his crimes; the Emperor detained Shaoliang at the Guest Reception Office, intending to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When dismissed, he traveled to the capital but received no appointment. Indignant at Zai's lawlessness, he submitted a memorial discussing his crimes. The emperor detained Shaoliang at the Guest Reception Office, intending to investigate the matter.

sentences.zh: 其友韋頌者候之，漏言於陸珽。

translations.literal: His friend Wei Song waited on him and leaked the words to Lu Ting.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Wei Song waited on him and leaked the words to Lu Ting.

sentences.zh: 載召珽問知之，乃奏下少良御史臺，劾其漏禁中語，並與頌、珽論殺之。

translations.literal: Zai summoned Ting and questioned him until he knew; he then memorialized to send Shaoliang down to the Censorate, impeaching him for leaking palace speech, and had Song and Ting tried and executed together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zai summoned Ting and questioned him until he knew. He then memorialized to send Shaoliang down to the Censorate, impeaching him for leaking palace speech, and had Song and Ting tried and executed together with him.

sentences.zh: 珽，善經子，與頌及少良善，又狎載子弟親黨，故載廉得其謀。

translations.literal: Ting was the son of Shan Jing; he was friendly with Song and Shaoliang, and also intimate with Zai's sons, followers, and kinsmen, and therefore Zai gradually learned of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was the son of Shan Jing. He was friendly with Song and Shaoliang, and also intimate with Zai's sons, followers, and kinsmen, and therefore Zai gradually learned of the plot.

sentences.zh: 初，載盛時，人皆疾厭之。

translations.literal: From the first, in Zai's days of power, everyone loathed and detested him.
translations.idiomatic: From the first, in Zai's days of power, everyone loathed and detested him.

sentences.zh: 大歷八年，有晉州男子郇謨以麻總發，持竹笥、葦席，行哭長安東市，人問之，曰：「我有字三十，欲以獻上，字言一事，即不中，以笥貯屍，席裹而棄之。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali, a man of Jin Prefecture named Xun Mo, with hemp binding his hair, carrying a bamboo chest and a reed mat, walked weeping through the Eastern Market of Chang'an; when people asked him, he said: "I have thirty characters I wish to present to the Emperor; each character speaks of one matter; if I am not accepted, I will store my corpse in the chest and wrap it in the mat and cast it away.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dali, a man of Jin Prefecture named Xun Mo, with hemp binding his hair, carrying a bamboo chest and a reed mat, walked weeping through the Eastern Market of Chang'an. When people asked him, he said: "I have thirty characters I wish to present to the emperor; each character speaks of one matter. If I am not accepted, I will store my corpse in the chest and wrap it in the mat and cast it away.

sentences.zh: 京兆以聞，帝召見，賜以衣，館內客省，問狀，多譏切載。

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Governor reported it; the Emperor summoned him for audience, granted him clothing, lodged him in the Inner Guest Reception Office, questioned him on the matter, and much of what he said satirized and criticized Zai.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan governor reported it. The emperor summoned him for audience, granted him clothing, lodged him in the Inner Guest Reception Office, questioned him on the matter, and much of what he said satirized and criticized Zai.

sentences.zh: 其言「團」者，願罷諸州團練使，其言「監」者，請罷諸道監軍，大抵類此。

translations.literal: Where he spoke of "regiment," he wished to abolish the regimental training commissioners of the various prefectures; where he spoke of "supervisor," he requested abolishing the circuit military supervisors; most of his points were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Where he spoke of "regiment," he wished to abolish the regimental training commissioners of the various prefectures; where he spoke of "supervisor," he requested abolishing the circuit military supervisors. Most of his points were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 先是，天下兵興，凡要州權署團練、刺史。

translations.literal: Previously, when warfare arose throughout the empire, all important prefectures were provisionally given regimental training commissioners and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when warfare arose throughout the empire, all important prefectures were provisionally given regimental training commissioners and prefects.

sentences.zh: 載用事，授刺史者悉帶團練以悅人心，故謨指而刺雲。

translations.literal: When Zai held power, all those appointed prefect also carried regimental training duties to please people's hearts; therefore Mo pointed at this and satirized it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai held power, all those appointed prefect also carried regimental training duties to please people's hearts; therefore Mo pointed at this and satirized it.

sentences.zh: 王縉，字夏卿，本太原祁人，後客河中。

translations.literal: Wang Jin, styled Xiaqing, was originally a native of Qi in Taiyuan, and later lived as a guest in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, courtesy name Xiaqing, was originally from Qi in Taiyuan and later lived as a guest in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少好學，與兄維俱以名聞。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; he and his elder brother Wei were both renowned.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning; he and his elder brother Wei were both renowned.

sentences.zh: 舉草澤、文辭清麗科上第，歷侍御史、武部員外郎。

translations.literal: He passed the Hidden Talents and Elegant Literary Composition examinations with highest rank, and served successively as Attending Censor and Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Hidden Talents and Elegant Literary Composition examinations with highest rank and served successively as attending censor and vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，擢太原少尹，佐李光弼，以功加憲部侍郎，遷兵部。

translations.literal: During the Lushan rebellion, he was promoted to Vice Governor of Taiyuan and assisted Li Guangbi; for merit he was made Vice Minister of Justice and transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: During the Lushan rebellion, he was promoted to vice governor of Taiyuan and assisted Li Guangbi. For merit he was made vice minister of justice and transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 史朝義平，詔宣慰河北，使還有指，俄拜黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Shi Chaoyi was pacified, he was ordered to serve as Pacification Commissioner of Hebei; upon his return he had private instructions, and soon was appointed Vice Director of the Gate and Co-Signatory Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Chaoyi was pacified, he was ordered to serve as pacification commissioner of Hebei. Upon his return he had private instructions, and soon was appointed vice director of the Gate and co-signatory director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 進侍中，持節都統河南、淮西、山南東道諸節度行營事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Palace Attendant and given the staff of authority as Overall Commander of the field headquarters of the Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to palace attendant and given the staff of authority as overall commander of the field headquarters of the Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuits.

sentences.zh: 辭侍中，加東都留守。

translations.literal: He declined the post of Palace Attendant and was instead made Eastern Capital governor.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post of palace attendant and was instead made governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜河南副元帥，損軍資錢四十萬緡，營完宮室。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was appointed Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Henan, contributed four hundred thousand strings of military funds, and completed the palace buildings.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, he was appointed deputy commander-in-chief of Henan, contributed four hundred thousand strings of military funds, and completed the palace buildings.

sentences.zh: 朱希彩殺李懷仙也，詔拜盧龍節度使，至幽州，委軍於希彩乃還。

translations.literal: When Zhu Xicai killed Li Huaixian, he was ordered appointed Military Commissioner of Lulong; arriving at Youzhou, he entrusted the army to Xicai and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xicai killed Li Huaixian, he was ordered appointed military commissioner of Lulong. Arriving at Youzhou, he entrusted the army to Xicai and then returned.

sentences.zh: 會辛雲京卒，兼領河東節度，讓還河南副元帥、東都留守。

translations.literal: When Xin Yunjing died, he concurrently took command of the Hedong military commission, then yielded and returned to his posts as Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Henan and Eastern Capital governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin Yunjing died, he concurrently took command of the Hedong military commission, then yielded and returned to his posts as deputy commander-in-chief of Henan and governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 太原將王無縱、張奉璋恃功，以縉儒者易之，不如律令，縉斬以徇，諸將股栗。

translations.literal: The Taiyuan generals Wang Wuzong and Zhang Fengzhang, relying on their merit, considered Jin a mere scholar easy to deal with and failed to obey laws and regulations; Jin executed them as a warning, and the other generals trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiyuan generals Wang Wuzong and Zhang Fengzhang, relying on their merit, considered Jin a mere scholar easy to deal with and failed to obey laws and regulations. Jin executed them as a warning, and the other generals trembled in fear.

sentences.zh: 再歲還，以本官復知政事。

translations.literal: After two years he returned and resumed governance of state affairs in his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he returned and resumed governance of state affairs in his former office.

sentences.zh: 時元載專朝，天子拱手，縉曲意附離，無敢忤。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Zai monopolized the court; the Son of Heaven held his hands together in deference; Jin bent his will to attach himself and dared not oppose.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuan Zai monopolized the court; the Son of Heaven held his hands together in deference. Jin bent his will to attach himself and dared not oppose.

sentences.zh: 又恃才多所狎侮，雖載亦疾其淩靳也。

translations.literal: He also relied on his talent and often treated others with familiar contempt; even Zai resented his overbearing arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: He also relied on his talent and often treated others with familiar contempt; even Zai resented his overbearing arrogance.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹黎幹數論執，載惡之，縉折幹曰：「尹，南方孤生，安曉朝廷事？」

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Governor Li Gan repeatedly argued stubbornly; Zai hated him; Jin cut Gan down, saying: "Governor, you are a lone scholar from the south—how would you understand court affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan governor Li Gan repeatedly argued stubbornly; Zai hated him. Jin cut Gan down, saying: "Governor, you are a lone scholar from the south—how would you understand court affairs?"

sentences.zh: 縉素奉佛，不茹葷食肉，晚節尤謹。

translations.literal: Jin had long devoted himself to Buddhism, abstaining from meat, and in his later years was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had long devoted himself to Buddhism, abstaining from meat, and in his later years was especially strict.

sentences.zh: 妻死，以道政裏第為佛祠，諸道節度、觀察使來朝，必邀至其所，諷令出財佐營作。

translations.literal: When his wife died, he made his mansion in Daozheng Ward into a Buddhist shrine; whenever military commissioners and regional inspectors from the circuits came to court, he always invited them to his place and hinted that they should contribute funds to help with construction.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife died, he made his mansion in Daozheng Ward into a Buddhist shrine. Whenever military commissioners and regional inspectors from the circuits came to court, he always invited them to his place and hinted that they should contribute funds to help with construction.

sentences.zh: 初，代宗喜祠祀，而未重浮屠法，每從容問所以然，縉與元載盛陳福業報應，帝意向之。

translations.literal: Initially, Emperor Daizong delighted in sacrificial rites but had not yet valued Buddhist law; he would casually ask the reasons; Jin and Yuan Zai lavishly expounded on karmic merit and retribution, and the Emperor's inclination turned toward it.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Emperor Daizong delighted in sacrificial rites but had not yet valued Buddhist law. He would casually ask the reasons, and Jin and Yuan Zai lavishly expounded on karmic merit and retribution. The emperor's inclination turned toward it.

sentences.zh: 繇是禁中祀佛，諷唄齋薰，號「內道場」，引內沙門日百餘，饌供珍滋，出入乘廄馬，度支具稟給。

translations.literal: From this the inner palace worshipped Buddha, with chanting, fasting, and incense, called the "Inner Way-Place"; more than a hundred inner-court monks were brought in daily, with sumptuous food offerings; they came and went riding stable horses, and the Ministry of Revenue supplied their rations.
translations.idiomatic: From this the inner palace worshipped Buddha, with chanting, fasting, and incense, in what was called the "Inner Way-Place." More than a hundred inner-court monks were brought in daily, with sumptuous food offerings. They came and went riding stable horses, and the Ministry of Revenue supplied their rations.

sentences.zh: 或夷狄入寇，必合眾沙門誦《護國仁王經》為禳厭，幸其去，則橫加錫與，不知紀極。

translations.literal: When barbarians invaded, all the monks would be assembled to recite the Sutra of the Humane Kings Who Protect the Nation as a rite of exorcism; when they fortunately departed, lavish rewards were heaped upon them beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: When barbarians invaded, all the monks would be assembled to recite the Sutra of the Humane Kings Who Protect the Nation as a rite of exorcism. When they fortunately departed, lavish rewards were heaped upon them beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 胡人官至卿監、封國公者，著籍禁省，勢傾公王，群居賴寵，更相淩奪，凡京畿上田美產，多歸浮屠。

translations.literal: Foreigners who reached the ranks of minister and supervisor or were enfeoffed as dukes of states were registered in the inner palace offices; their power overshadowed dukes and princes; living in groups they relied on favor and plundered one another; all the finest fields and estates of the capital region mostly passed to the Buddhist clergy.
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners who reached the ranks of minister and supervisor or were enfeoffed as dukes of states were registered in the inner palace offices. Their power overshadowed dukes and princes. Living in groups they relied on favor and plundered one another, and all the finest fields and estates of the capital region mostly passed to the Buddhist clergy.

sentences.zh: 雖藏奸宿亂踵相逮，而帝終不悟，詔天下官司不得箠辱僧尼。

translations.literal: Although hidden treachery and long-standing disorder followed one after another, the Emperor never understood; an edict ordered that officials throughout the empire must not beat or humiliate monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: Although hidden treachery and long-standing disorder followed one after another, the emperor never understood. An edict ordered that officials throughout the empire must not beat or humiliate monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 初，五臺山祠鑄銅為瓦，金塗之，費億萬計。

translations.literal: Initially, the Wutai Mountain shrine cast copper into tiles and gilded them, costing hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, the Wutai Mountain shrine cast copper into tiles and gilded them, costing hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 縉給中書符，遣浮屠數十輩行州縣，斂丐貲貨。

translations.literal: Jin issued Chancellery documents and dispatched several dozen Buddhist monks to travel through prefectures and counties, collecting alms and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Jin issued Chancellery documents and dispatched several dozen Buddhist monks to travel through prefectures and counties, collecting alms and goods.

sentences.zh: 縉為上言：「國家慶祚靈長，福報所馮，雖時多難，無足道者。

translations.literal: Jin said to the Emperor: "The state's fortune and mandate are spiritually enduring, supported by karmic reward; though the times have many hardships, they are not worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said to the emperor: "The state's fortune and mandate are spiritually enduring, supported by karmic reward. Though the times have many hardships, they are not worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 祿山、思明毒亂方煽，而皆有子禍，仆固懷恩臨亂而踣，西戎內寇，未及擊輒去，非人事也。」

translations.literal: Lushan and Siming's poisonous rebellion was just blazing forth, yet both suffered calamity through their sons; Pugu Huai'en faced rebellion and fell; the Western barbarians invaded within the borders, and before they could be struck they departed—these were not matters of human agency.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan and Siming's poisonous rebellion was just blazing forth, yet both suffered calamity through their sons. Pugu Huai'en faced rebellion and fell. The Western barbarians invaded within the borders, and before they could be struck they departed—these were not matters of human agency.

sentences.zh: 故帝信愈篤。

translations.literal: Therefore the Emperor's faith grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the emperor's faith grew ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 七月望日，宮中造盂蘭盆，綴飾镠飲琲，設高祖以下七聖位，幡節、衣冠皆具，各以帝號識其幡，自禁內分詣道佛祠，鐃吹鼓舞，奔走相屬。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the palace made Ullambana offerings, adorned with gold and jade ornaments; seats were set for the seven sages from Emperor Gaozu downward, with banners, insignia, and robes all complete; each banner was marked with an imperial title; from within the Forbidden City they were dispatched separately to Daoist and Buddhist shrines, with gongs, drums, and dancing, people rushing one after another.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the palace made Ullambana offerings adorned with gold and jade ornaments. Seats were set for the seven sages from Emperor Gaozu downward, with banners, insignia, and robes all complete, each banner marked with an imperial title. From within the Forbidden City they were dispatched separately to Daoist and Buddhist shrines, with gongs, drums, and dancing, people rushing one after another.

sentences.zh: 是日立仗，百官班光順門，奉迎導從，歲以為常。

translations.literal: On that day the guard was drawn up; all officials lined up at Guangshun Gate to receive and escort the procession; this became an annual custom.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the guard was drawn up; all officials lined up at Guangshun Gate to receive and escort the procession. This became an annual custom.

sentences.zh: 群臣承風，皆言生死報應，故人事置而不脩，大歷政刑，日以堙陵，由縉與元載、杜鴻漸倡之也。

translations.literal: The ministers followed the trend, all speaking of karmic retribution in life and death; therefore human affairs were set aside and not cultivated; during the Dali era government and punishments daily sank into decline—this was initiated by Jin together with Yuan Zai and Du Hongjian.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers followed the trend, all speaking of karmic retribution in life and death. Human affairs were set aside and not cultivated; during the Dali era government and punishments daily sank into decline—this was initiated by Jin together with Yuan Zai and Du Hongjian.

sentences.zh: 性貪冒，縱親戚尼甘招納財賄，猥屑相稽，若市賈然。

translations.literal: By nature he was greedy and grasping; he allowed kinsmen, nuns, and sweet-talkers to solicit bribes; petty matters were haggled over as if in a marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was greedy and grasping. He allowed kinsmen, nuns, and sweet-talkers to solicit bribes, and petty matters were haggled over as if in a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 及敗，劉晏等鞫其罪，同載論死，晏曰：「重刑再覆，有國常典，況大臣乎！

translations.literal: When he fell, Liu Yan and others interrogated his crimes; together with Zai he was sentenced to death; Yan said: "Heavy punishment applied twice is a constant rule of state—how much more for a great minister!
translations.idiomatic: When he fell, Liu Yan and others interrogated his crimes. Together with Zai he was sentenced to death. Yan said: "Heavy punishment applied twice is a constant rule of state—how much more for a great minister!

sentences.zh: 法有首從，不容俱死。」

translations.literal: The law distinguishes principal and accomplice; they cannot all be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The law distinguishes principal and accomplice; they cannot all be put to death.

sentences.zh: 於是以聞，上憫其耄，不加刑，乃貶括州刺史。

translations.literal: This was reported upward; the Emperor pitied his advanced age and did not impose punishment, but demoted him to Prefect of Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: This was reported upward. The emperor pitied his advanced age and did not impose punishment, but demoted him to prefect of Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with duties at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, he was transferred to mentor of the heir apparent, with duties at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 建中二年死，年八十二。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Jianzhong, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Jianzhong, aged eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 黎幹，戎州人。

translations.literal: Li Gan was a native of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan was a native of Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 善星緯術，得待詔翰林，擢累諫議大夫，封壽春公。

translations.idiomatic: Your subject maintains that in the Spring and Autumn Annals, "great affairs in the Grand Temple"—though called "great," can this mean sacrifice to Heaven?

translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: the beginning of all things is Heaven;

sentences.zh: 人之始，祖也；

translations.literal: the beginning of humanity is the ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: the beginning of humanity is the ancestor;

sentences.zh: 日之始，至也。

translations.literal: the beginning of the day is the solstice.
translations.idiomatic: the beginning of the day is the solstice.

sentences.zh: 掃地而祭，則質；

translations.literal: Sweeping the ground to sacrifice shows simplicity;
translations.idiomatic: Sweeping the ground to sacrifice shows simplicity;

sentences.zh: 器用陶匏，則性；

translations.literal: using pottery and gourds for vessels shows naturalness;
translations.idiomatic: using pottery and gourds for vessels shows naturalness;

sentences.zh: 牲用犢，則誠；

translations.literal: using a calf for the victim shows sincerity;
translations.idiomatic: using a calf for the victim shows sincerity;

sentences.zh: 兆於南郊，則就陽。

translations.literal: establishing the altar in the southern suburb draws near to yang.
translations.idiomatic: establishing the altar in the southern suburb draws near to yang.

sentences.zh: 至尊至質，不敢同於先祖也。」

translations.literal: The most exalted and most simple—one dares not treat it the same as the former ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The most exalted and most simple—one dares not treat it the same as the former ancestors.

sentences.zh: 《白虎通議》曰：『祭天歲一者何？

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Discussions in the White Tiger Hall says: "Why is Heaven sacrificed to once a year?"
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Discussions in the White Tiger Hall says: "Why is Heaven sacrificed to once a year?"

sentences.zh: 事之不敢黷也。』

translations.literal: "One dares not be excessive in the matter."
translations.idiomatic: "One dares not be excessive in the matter."

sentences.zh: 故因歲之陽氣始達而祭之。

translations.literal: Therefore one sacrifices when the year's yang qi first reaches fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one sacrifices when the year's yang qi first reaches fullness.

sentences.zh: 今一歲四祭，黷莫大焉。

translations.literal: Now to sacrifice four times in one year—excess could be no greater.
translations.idiomatic: Now to sacrifice four times in one year—excess could be no greater.

sentences.zh: 上帝五帝，祀闕不舉，怠孰甚焉？

translations.literal: August Heaven and the Five Emperors—if sacrifices are omitted and not performed, neglect could be no greater.
translations.idiomatic: August Heaven and the Five Emperors—if sacrifices are omitted and not performed, neglect could be no greater.

sentences.zh: 黷與怠，皆失也。

translations.literal: Excess and neglect are both failures.
translations.idiomatic: Excess and neglect are both failures.

sentences.zh: 臣聞親有限，祖有常，聖人制禮不以情變。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that kinship has limits and ancestors have constants; the sages established ritual and did not alter it according to emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that kinship has limits and ancestors have constants. The sages established ritual and did not alter it according to emotion.

sentences.zh: 唐家累聖，歷祀百年，非不知景帝為始封。

translations.literal: The Tang has accumulated sage emperors and performed sacrifices for a hundred years—it is not that they did not know Emperor Jing was the first enfeoffed lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang has accumulated sage emperors and performed sacrifices for a hundred years—it is not that they did not know Emperor Jing was the first enfeoffed lord.

sentences.zh: 當時通儒鉅工尊高祖以配天，宗太宗以配上帝，人神克厭，為日既久。

translations.literal: At that time, eminent scholars and great masters honored Gaozu as paired with Heaven and venerated Taizong as paired with August Heaven; gods and men were both satisfied, and this had lasted a long time.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, eminent scholars and great masters honored Gaozu as paired with Heaven and venerated Taizong as paired with August Heaven. Gods and men were both satisfied, and this had lasted a long time.

sentences.zh: 乃今以神堯降侑含樞紐，而太宗仍配上帝，則樞紐上帝佐也。

translations.literal: Now to demote the Divine Yao to serve as assistant at the hub, while Taizong still pairs with August Heaven—then the hub is assistant to August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Now to demote the Divine Yao to serve as assistant at the hub, while Taizong still pairs with August Heaven—then the hub becomes assistant to August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 以子先父，非天地祖宗之意。」

translations.literal: To put the son before the father is not the intent of Heaven, Earth, and the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: To put the son before the father is not the intent of Heaven, Earth, and the ancestors."

sentences.zh: 八曰：「景皇帝非造我區夏，不得與夏之禹、商之契、周之稷、漢高帝、魏武帝、晉宣帝、唐神堯皇帝並功，則陟配圜丘，上與天匹，曾謂圜丘不如林放乎？」

translations.literal: Eighth: "Emperor Jing did not create our realm and cannot be ranked with Yu of Xia, Qi of Shang, Ji of Zhou, Emperor Gaodi of Han, Emperor Wu of Wei, Emperor Xuan of Jin, and the Divine Yao Emperor of Tang in merit; then to ascend and pair at the Round Mound, matching Heaven above—can one say the Round Mound is inferior to Lin Fang?"
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: "Emperor Jing did not create our realm and cannot be ranked with Yu of Xia, Qi of Shang, Ji of Zhou, Emperor Gaodi of Han, Emperor Wu of Wei, Emperor Xuan of Jin, and the Divine Yao Emperor of Tang in merit. To ascend and pair at the Round Mound, matching Heaven above—can one say the Round Mound is inferior to Lin Fang?"

sentences.zh: 九曰：「魏以武帝、晉以宣帝為始祖者，夫操與懿皆人傑也。

translations.literal: Ninth: "Wei took Emperor Wu and Jin took Emperor Xuan as Grand Ancestors—Cao Cao and Sima Yi were both outstanding men.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth: "Wei took Emperor Wu and Jin took Emperor Xuan as Grand Ancestors—Cao Cao and Sima Yi were both outstanding men.

sentences.zh: 擁天下強兵，挾弱主，制海內之命，名雖為臣，勢實為君，後世因之以成帝業，尊而祖之，不亦可乎？」

translations.literal: They held the empire's strong armies, controlled weak rulers, and commanded the fate of all within the seas; in name they were subjects, but in power they were truly lords; later generations followed them to achieve imperial enterprise—is it not acceptable to honor and make them Grand Ancestors?"
translations.idiomatic: They held the empire's strong armies, controlled weak rulers, and commanded the fate of all within the seas. In name they were subjects, but in power they were truly lords. Later generations followed them to achieve imperial enterprise—is it not acceptable to honor and make them Grand Ancestors?"

sentences.zh: 十曰：「神堯拯隋室之亂，振臂大呼，濟人塗炭，汛掃蕩攘，群兇無餘，出入不數年而成王業，漢祖之功不能加焉。

translations.literal: Tenth: "The Divine Yao rescued the Sui from chaos, raised his arm and cried out, saved people from fire and water, swept and cleared away all opposition, leaving the wicked with nothing; entering and departing within a few years he achieved royal enterprise—the merit of Han's founder cannot surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth: "The Divine Yao rescued the Sui from chaos, raised his arm and cried out, saved people from fire and water, swept and cleared away all opposition, leaving the wicked with nothing. Within a few years he achieved royal enterprise—the merit of Han's founder cannot surpass this.

sentences.zh: 夏以禹，漢以高帝，我以神堯為始祖，訂夏法漢，於義何嫌？

translations.literal: Xia took Yu, Han took Gaodi, we take the Divine Yao as Grand Ancestor, following Xia and modeling Han—what objection is there in principle?
translations.idiomatic: Xia took Yu, Han took Gaodi, we take the Divine Yao as Grand Ancestor, following Xia and modeling Han—what objection is there in principle?

sentences.zh: 今頎、崇敬革天對，易祖廟，事之大者不稽於古，難以疑文僻說定之。

translations.literal: Now Qi and Chongjing alter Heaven's pairing and change the ancestral temples—matters of such magnitude cannot be decided without consulting antiquity, and cannot be settled by doubtful texts and eccentric arguments.
translations.idiomatic: Now Qi and Chongjing alter Heaven's pairing and change the ancestral temples—matters of such magnitude cannot be decided without consulting antiquity, and cannot be settled by doubtful texts and eccentric arguments.

sentences.zh: 臣官以諫為名，不敢不盡愚。」

translations.literal: Your subject's office is named for remonstrance; I dare not fail to offer my full foolish counsel."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's office is named for remonstrance; I dare not fail to offer my full foolish counsel."

sentences.zh: 議聞，代宗不韙其言。

translations.literal: When the memorial was heard, Emperor Daizong did not approve his words.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was heard, Emperor Daizong did not approve his words.

sentences.zh: 其後名儒大議，而景帝配天卒著於禮。

translations.literal: Afterward eminent scholars debated at length, and Emperor Jing's pairing with Heaven was ultimately established in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward eminent scholars debated at length, and Emperor Jing's pairing with Heaven was ultimately established in ritual.

sentences.zh: 俄遷京兆尹，頗以治稱。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and gained some reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and gained some reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 京師苦樵薪乏，幹度開漕渠，興南山谷口，尾入於苑，以便運載。

translations.literal: The capital suffered from a shortage of firewood and kindling; Gan surveyed and opened a canal, starting from the mouth of the southern mountain valley and ending in the imperial park, to facilitate transport.
translations.idiomatic: The capital suffered from a shortage of firewood and kindling. Gan surveyed and opened a canal, starting from the mouth of the southern mountain valley and ending in the imperial park, to facilitate transport.

sentences.zh: 帝為禦安福門觀之。

translations.literal: The Emperor went to Anfu Gate to observe it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to Anfu Gate to observe it.

sentences.zh: 幹密具同船作倡優水嬉，冀以媚帝。

translations.literal: Gan secretly prepared boats with actors performing water entertainments, hoping to please the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Gan secretly prepared boats with actors performing water entertainments, hoping to please the emperor.

sentences.zh: 久之，渠不就。

translations.literal: After a long time, the canal was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, the canal was not completed.

sentences.zh: 俄改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩敗，坐交通，出為桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: When Yu Chao'en fell, Gan was implicated for association with him and sent out as Regional Inspector of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chao'en fell, Gan was implicated for association with him and sent out as regional inspector of Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 大歷八年，復召為京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali, he was recalled as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dali, he was recalled as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，幹造土龍，自與巫覡對舞，彌月不應。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought; Gan made an earthen dragon and danced facing shamans himself; for a full month there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was great drought. Gan made an earthen dragon and danced facing shamans himself. For a full month there was no response.

sentences.zh: 又禱孔子廟，帝笑曰：「丘之禱久矣。」

translations.literal: He also prayed at the Confucius temple; the Emperor laughed and said: "Qiu has prayed for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He also prayed at the Confucius temple. The emperor laughed and said: "Qiu has prayed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 使毀土龍，帝減膳節用，既而霪雨。

translations.literal: He ordered the earthen dragon destroyed; the Emperor reduced his meals and curtailed expenses, and soon torrential rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the earthen dragon destroyed. The emperor reduced his meals and curtailed expenses, and soon torrential rain fell.

sentences.zh: 十三年，涇水擁隔，請開鄭、白支渠，復秦、漢故道以溉民田，廢碾硙八十餘所。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Jing River was blocked; he requested opening the Zheng and Bai branch canals, restoring the Qin and Han old channels to irrigate the people's fields, and abolishing more than eighty water mills.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, the Jing River was blocked. He requested opening the Zheng and Bai branch canals, restoring the Qin and Han old channels to irrigate the people's fields, and abolishing more than eighty water mills.

sentences.zh: 幹性貪暴，既復用，不暇念治，專徇財色，附會嬖近，挾左道希主恩，帝甚惑之。

translations.literal: Gan was greedy and violent by nature; once reappointed, he had no time to think of governance, devoted himself solely to wealth and women, attached himself to favorites, and relied on heterodox ways to seek the Emperor's favor—the Emperor was greatly deluded by him.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was greedy and violent by nature. Once reappointed, he had no time to think of governance, devoted himself solely to wealth and women, attached himself to favorites, and relied on heterodox ways to seek the emperor's favor. The emperor was greatly deluded by him.

sentences.zh: 德宗在東宮，幹與宦者特進劉忠翼陰謀，幾危宗嗣。

translations.literal: When Dezong was in the Eastern Palace, Gan and the eunuch Special Advancement Liu Zhongyi plotted secretly, nearly endangering the imperial succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was in the Eastern Palace, Gan and the eunuch Special Advancement Liu Zhongyi plotted secretly, nearly endangering the imperial succession.

sentences.zh: 及即位，又詭道希進，密乘車謁忠翼。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne, Gan again used devious means hoping for advancement, secretly riding in a carriage to visit Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne, Gan again used devious means hoping for advancement, secretly riding in a carriage to visit Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 事覺，除名長流，既行，市人數百群噪投礫從之，俄賜死藍田驛。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered, he was stripped of office and exiled far away; as he departed, several hundred townspeople gathered, shouting and throwing stones at him; soon he was granted death at Lantian Post.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was discovered, he was stripped of office and exiled far away. As he departed, several hundred townspeople gathered, shouting and throwing stones at him. Soon he was granted death at Lantian Post.

sentences.zh: 忠翼本名清潭，與左衛將軍董秀皆有寵於代宗。

translations.literal: Zhongyi's original name was Qingtan; he and Left Guard General Dong Xiu both enjoyed favor with Emperor Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi's original name was Qingtan. He and Left Guard General Dong Xiu both enjoyed favor with Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 當盛時，爵賞在其口吻，掊冒財賄，貲產累皆巨萬。

translations.literal: At the height of their power, ranks and rewards issued from their lips; they plundered and seized bribes, and their accumulated wealth reached tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of their power, ranks and rewards issued from their lips. They plundered and seized bribes, and their accumulated wealth reached tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 至是，積前罪，並及誅。

translations.literal: At this time, accumulated with their previous crimes, both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, accumulated with their previous crimes, both were executed.

sentences.zh: 楊炎，字公南，鳳翔天興人。

translations.literal: Yang Yan, styled Gongnan, was a native of Tianxing in Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan, courtesy name Gongnan, came from Tianxing in Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖大寶，武德初為龍門令，劉武周攻之，死於守，贈全節侯。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dabao served as Magistrate of Longmen in the early Wude era; when Liu Wuzhou attacked, he died defending the city and was posthumously granted Marquis of Quanjie.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dabao served as magistrate of Longmen in the early Wude era. When Liu Wuzhou attacked, he died defending the city and was posthumously granted Marquis of Quanjie.

sentences.zh: 祖哲，以孝行稱。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhe was renowned for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhe was renowned for filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 父播，舉進士，退居求誌，玄宗召拜諫議大夫，棄官歸養。

translations.literal: His father Bo passed the jinshi examination, retired to seek his will, was summoned and appointed Remonstrance Officer by Emperor Xuanzong, and resigned office to return home and care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bo passed the jinshi examination, retired to seek his will, was summoned and appointed remonstrance officer by Emperor Xuanzong, and resigned office to return home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，即家拜散騎常侍，號玄靖先生。

translations.literal: In Emperor Suzong's time, he was appointed Palace Attendant at his home and styled Master Xuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Suzong's time, he was appointed palace attendant at his home and styled Master Xuanjing.

sentences.zh: 炎美須眉，峻風宇，文藻雄蔚，然豪爽尚氣。

translations.literal: Yan had handsome beard and eyebrows, a stern bearing, and literary talent that was bold and luxuriant, yet he was also open and generous, valuing spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had handsome beard and eyebrows, a stern bearing, and literary talent that was bold and luxuriant, yet he was also open and generous, valuing spirit.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使呂崇賁辟掌書記。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Hexi Lü Chongben recruited him as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner of Hexi Lü Chongben recruited him as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 神烏令李太簡嘗醉辱之，炎令左右反接，搒二百餘，幾死，崇賁愛其才，不問。

translations.literal: Li Taijian, magistrate of Shenwu, once insulted him while drunk; Yan ordered his attendants to bind him with arms reversed and beat him more than two hundred strokes, nearly killing him; Chongben valued his talent and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Li Taijian, magistrate of Shenwu, once insulted him while drunk. Yan ordered his attendants to bind him with arms reversed and beat him more than two hundred strokes, nearly killing him. Chongben valued his talent and did not inquire.

sentences.zh: 李光弼表為判官，不應。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi memorialized for him as administrative aide; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi memorialized for him as administrative aide; he did not accept.

sentences.zh: 召拜起居舍人，固辭。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Attendant of Daily Affairs; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed attendant of daily affairs; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 父喪，廬墓側，號慕不廢聲，有紫芝白雀之祥，詔表其閭。

translations.literal: When his father died, he built a hut beside the tomb, wailing in grief without ceasing; there were auspicious signs of purple fungus and white sparrows; an edict marked his village.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he built a hut beside the tomb, wailing in grief without ceasing. There were auspicious signs of purple fungus and white sparrows, and an edict marked his village.

sentences.zh: 炎三世以孝行聞，至門樹六闕，古所未有。

translations.literal: Yan's three generations were renowned for filial conduct; at his gate stood six commemorative towers—unprecedented in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's three generations were renowned for filial conduct. At his gate stood six commemorative towers—unprecedented in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 終喪，為司勛員外郎，遷中書舍人，與常袞同時知制誥。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel Records, was transferred to Secretariat Draftsman, and concurrently with Chang Gun drafted imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he served as vice director in the Ministry of Personnel Records, was transferred to secretariat draftsman, and concurrently with Chang Gun drafted imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 袞長於除書，而炎善德音，自開元後言制詔者，稱「常楊」雲。

translations.literal: Gun excelled at appointment edicts, while Yan was skilled at benevolent pronouncements; from the Kaiyuan era onward, those who spoke of drafting edicts called them "Chang and Yang."
translations.idiomatic: Gun excelled at appointment edicts, while Yan was skilled at benevolent pronouncements. From the Kaiyuan era onward, those who spoke of drafting edicts called them "Chang and Yang."

sentences.zh: 宰相元載與炎同郡，炎又元出也，故擢炎吏部侍郎、史館脩撰。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yuan Zai was from the same commandery as Yan, and Yan was also Yuan's clansman by marriage; therefore Yan was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yuan Zai was from the same commandery as Yan, and Yan was also Yuan's clansman by marriage. Therefore Yan was promoted to vice minister of personnel and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 載當國，陰擇才可代己者，引以自近，初得禮部侍郎劉單，會卒，復取吏部侍郎薛邕，邕坐事貶，後得炎，親重無比。

translations.literal: When Zai governed the state, he secretly selected talented men who could replace him and drew them near; he first obtained Vice Minister of Rites Liu Shan, who happened to die; then he took Vice Minister of Personnel Xue Yong, who was demoted for an offense; afterward he obtained Yan, treating him with unmatched intimacy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai governed the state, he secretly selected talented men who could replace him and drew them near. He first obtained Vice Minister of Rites Liu Shan, who happened to die. Then he took Vice Minister of Personnel Xue Yong, who was demoted for an offense. Afterward he obtained Yan, treating him with unmatched intimacy and favor.

sentences.zh: 會載敗，坐貶道州司馬。

translations.literal: When Zai fell, Yan was implicated and demoted to Military Staff Officer of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai fell, Yan was implicated and demoted to military staff officer of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗在東宮，雅知其名，又嘗得炎所為《李楷洛碑》，寘於壁，日諷玩之。

translations.literal: When Dezong was in the Eastern Palace, he already knew Yan's name by reputation; he had also once obtained Yan's "Stele for Li Kailuo," placed it on the wall, and daily recited and admired it.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was in the Eastern Palace, he already knew Yan's name by reputation. He had also once obtained Yan's "Stele for Li Kailuo," placed it on the wall, and daily recited and admired it.

sentences.zh: 及即位，崔祐甫薦炎可器任，即拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Cui Youfu recommended Yan as capable of appointment; he was immediately appointed Vice Director of the Gate and Co-Signatory Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended the throne, Cui Youfu recommended Yan as capable of appointment. He was immediately appointed vice director of the Gate and co-signatory director of the Chancellery and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 舊制，天下財賦皆入左藏庫，而太府四時以數聞，尚書比部覆出納，舉無幹欺。

translations.literal: Under the old system, all the empire's revenues and taxes entered the Left Treasury, while the Court of the Imperial Treasury reported the figures each season, and the Ministry's Comparison Section reviewed receipts and disbursements—altogether without interference or fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, all the empire's revenues and taxes entered the Left Treasury, while the Court of the Imperial Treasury reported the figures each season, and the Ministry's Comparison Section reviewed receipts and disbursements—altogether without interference or fraud.

sentences.zh: 及第五琦為度支、鹽鐵使，京師豪將求取無節，琦不能禁，乃悉租賦進大盈內庫。

translations.literal: When Diwu Qi served as Commissioner of Revenue and Salt and Iron, the capital's powerful generals demanded without restraint; Qi could not forbid them, and therefore sent all rents and taxes into the Great Abundance Inner Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Diwu Qi served as commissioner of revenue and salt and iron, the capital's powerful generals demanded without restraint. Qi could not forbid them, and therefore sent all rents and taxes into the Great Abundance Inner Treasury.

sentences.zh: 天子以給取為便，故不復出。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven found it convenient to take and supply from there, and therefore did not return revenues to the regular treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven found it convenient to take and supply from there, and therefore did not return revenues to the regular treasury.

sentences.zh: 自是天下公賦為人君私藏，有司不得計贏少。

translations.literal: From then on the empire's public taxes became the ruler's private store, and responsible offices could not calculate surplus or deficit.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the empire's public taxes became the ruler's private store, and responsible offices could not calculate surplus or deficit.

sentences.zh: 而宦官以冗名持簿者三百人，奉給其間，根柢連結不可動。

translations.literal: Eunuchs holding ledgers under redundant titles numbered three hundred, receiving salaries from this fund; their roots were intertwined and could not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs holding ledgers under redundant titles numbered three hundred, receiving salaries from this fund. Their roots were intertwined and could not be moved.

sentences.zh: 及炎為相，言於帝曰：「財賦者，邦國大本，而生人之喉命，天下治亂重輕系焉。

translations.literal: When Yan became chief minister, he said to the Emperor: "Revenues and taxes are the great foundation of the state and the throat and life of the people; the weight of order and disorder in the empire depends on them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan became chief minister, he said to the emperor: "Revenues and taxes are the great foundation of the state and the throat and life of the people. The weight of order and disorder in the empire depends on them.

sentences.zh: 先朝權制，以中人領其職，五尺宦豎，操邦之柄，豐儉盈虛，雖大臣不得知，則無以計天下利害。

translations.literal: The previous court's expedient measure placed eunuchs in charge of this duty; five-foot palace attendants held the state's power; whether abundance or scarcity, surplus or deficit—even great ministers could not know—then there was no way to calculate the empire's benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: The previous court's expedient measure placed eunuchs in charge of this duty. Five-foot palace attendants held the state's power. Whether abundance or scarcity, surplus or deficit—even great ministers could not know—then there was no way to calculate the empire's benefit and harm.

sentences.zh: 陛下至德，惟人是恤，參計敝蠹，莫與斯甚。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's supreme virtue cares for the people; considering the accumulated corruption, nothing equals this in severity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's supreme virtue cares for the people. Considering the accumulated corruption, nothing equals this in severity.

sentences.zh: 臣請出之，以歸有司。

translations.literal: Your subject requests removing it and returning it to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject requests removing it and returning it to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 度宮中經費一歲幾何，量數奉入，不敢以闕。

translations.literal: Estimate how much the palace requires in a year, measure the amount to be supplied, and dare not allow any shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Estimate how much the palace requires in a year, measure the amount to be supplied, and dare not allow any shortfall.

sentences.zh: 如此，然後可以議政，惟陛下審察。」

translations.literal: Only thus can state affairs be deliberated—may Your Majesty examine this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus can state affairs be deliberated—may Your Majesty examine this carefully.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃詔歲中裁取以入大盈，度支具數先聞。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued that within the year only the measured amount would be taken into the Great Abundance Treasury, with the Ministry of Revenue reporting the figures in advance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued that within the year only the measured amount would be taken into the Great Abundance Treasury, with the Ministry of Revenue reporting the figures in advance.

sentences.zh: 初，定令有租賦庸調法，自開元承平久，不為版籍，法度玩敝。

translations.literal: Initially, the established code had the system of rent, tax, corvée, and cloth levy; since the long peace of Kaiyuan, household registers were not maintained, and the legal system fell into neglect and decay.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, the established code had the system of rent, tax, corvée, and cloth levy. Since the long peace of Kaiyuan, household registers were not maintained, and the legal system fell into neglect and decay.

sentences.zh: 而丁口轉死，田畝換易，貧富升降，悉非向時，而戶部歲以空文上之。

translations.literal: Household members died or moved away, fields changed hands, the rich and poor rose and fell—all unlike before—yet the Ministry of Revenue each year submitted empty documents.
translations.idiomatic: Household members died or moved away, fields changed hands, the rich and poor rose and fell—all unlike before—yet the Ministry of Revenue each year submitted empty documents.

sentences.zh: 又戍邊者，蠲其租、庸，六歲免歸。

translations.literal: Those garrisoning the frontier were exempted from rent and corvée, and after six years were released to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Those garrisoning the frontier were exempted from rent and corvée, and after six years were released to return home.

sentences.zh: 玄宗事夷狄，戍者多死，邊將諱不以聞，故貫籍不除。
