translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong campaigned against the barbarians; many garrison soldiers died, but frontier generals concealed this and did not report it, so the registers were not cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong campaigned against the barbarians. Many garrison soldiers died, but frontier generals concealed this and did not report it, so the registers were not cleared.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，王鉷為戶口使，方務聚斂，以其籍存而丁不在，是隱課不出，乃按舊籍，除當免者，積三十年，責其租、庸，人苦無告，故法遂大敝。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, Wang Hong served as Household Commissioner, devoted to gathering revenue; because registers remained while household members were absent, hidden taxes went uncollected; he therefore checked old registers, removed those who should have been exempt, accumulated thirty years, and demanded their rent and corvée; people suffered with no recourse, and thus the law fell into great decay.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era, Wang Hong served as household commissioner, devoted to gathering revenue. Because registers remained while household members were absent, hidden taxes went uncollected. He therefore checked old registers, removed those who should have been exempt, accumulated thirty years, and demanded their rent and corvée. People suffered with no recourse, and thus the law fell into great decay.

sentences.zh: 至德後，天下兵起，因以饑癘，百役並作，人戶雕耗，版圖空虛。

translations.literal: After Zhide, warfare arose throughout the empire, followed by famine and pestilence; a hundred levies were imposed together; households were depleted and registers emptied.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhide, warfare arose throughout the empire, followed by famine and pestilence. A hundred levies were imposed together; households were depleted and registers emptied.

sentences.zh: 軍國之用，仰給於度支、轉運使；

translations.literal: Military and state expenses relied on the commissioners of revenue and transport;
translations.idiomatic: Military and state expenses relied on the commissioners of revenue and transport;

sentences.zh: 四方征鎮，又自給於節度、都團練使。

translations.literal: the expeditionary garrisons of the four directions likewise supplied themselves through military commissioners and overall regimental training commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The expeditionary garrisons of the four directions likewise supplied themselves through military commissioners and overall regimental training commissioners.

sentences.zh: 賦斂之司數四，莫相統攝，綱目大壞。

translations.literal: Tax collection offices numbered four, none supervising one another; the overall system was greatly broken.
translations.idiomatic: Tax collection offices numbered four, none supervising one another. The overall system was greatly broken.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不能覆諸使，諸使不能覆諸州。

translations.literal: The court could not oversee the commissioners; the commissioners could not oversee the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The court could not oversee the commissioners; the commissioners could not oversee the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 四方貢獻，悉入內庫，權臣巧吏，因得旁緣，公托進獻，私為贓盜者，動萬萬計。

translations.literal: Tributes from all directions all entered the inner treasury; powerful ministers and clever clerks thereby gained side opportunities; those who publicly claimed to offer tribute but privately stole numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Tributes from all directions all entered the inner treasury. Powerful ministers and clever clerks thereby gained side opportunities. Those who publicly claimed to offer tribute but privately stole numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 河南、山東、荊襄、劍南重兵處，皆厚自奉養，王賦所入無幾。

translations.literal: In Henan, Shandong, Jingxiang, and Jiannan, where heavy troops were stationed, all richly maintained themselves; little of the imperial taxes reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan, Shandong, Jingxiang, and Jiannan, where heavy troops were stationed, all richly maintained themselves. Little of the imperial taxes reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 科斂凡數百名，廢者不削，重者不去，新舊仍積，不知其涯。

translations.literal: Tax items numbered several hundred; abolished ones were not cut, heavy ones were not removed; old and new accumulated together, with no knowing the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Tax items numbered several hundred. Abolished ones were not cut, heavy ones were not removed. Old and new accumulated together, with no knowing the limit.

sentences.zh: 百姓竭膏血，鬻親愛，旬輸月送，無有休息。

translations.literal: The common people exhausted their life's blood, sold their loved ones, paid every ten days and delivered every month, without rest.
translations.idiomatic: The common people exhausted their life's blood, sold their loved ones, paid every ten days and delivered every month, without rest.

sentences.zh: 吏因其苛，蠶食於人。

translations.literal: Officials, taking advantage of the harsh levies, devoured the people like silkworms eating mulberry leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, taking advantage of the harsh levies, devoured the people like silkworms eating mulberry leaves.

sentences.zh: 富人多丁者，以宦、學、釋、老得免，貧人無所入則丁存。

translations.literal: Rich men with many sons obtained exemption through office, study, Buddhism, or Daoism; poor men with no such entry remained registered for corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Rich men with many sons obtained exemption through office, study, Buddhism, or Daoism. Poor men with no such entry remained registered for corvée.

sentences.zh: 故課免於上，而賦增於下。

translations.literal: Thus exemptions appeared above while burdens increased below.
translations.idiomatic: Thus exemptions appeared above while burdens increased below.

sentences.zh: 是以天下殘瘁，蕩為浮人，鄉居地著者百不四五。

translations.literal: Therefore the empire was devastated; people drifted as vagrants; those settled in their native villages were not even four or five in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the empire was devastated. People drifted as vagrants. Those settled in their native villages were not even four or five in a hundred.

sentences.zh: 炎疾其敝，乃請為「兩稅法」以一其制。

translations.literal: Yan grieved at this decay and therefore requested the "Two Tax Law" to unify the system.
translations.idiomatic: Yan grieved at this decay and therefore requested the "Two Tax Law" to unify the system.

sentences.zh: 凡百役之費，一錢之斂，先度其數而賦於人，量出制入。

translations.literal: All expenses for corvée and all collections of cash would first be estimated in amount and then assessed on the people—measuring outflow to determine intake.
translations.idiomatic: All expenses for corvée and all collections of cash would first be estimated in amount and then assessed on the people—measuring outflow to determine intake.

sentences.zh: 戶無主客，以見居為簿；

translations.literal: Households would have no distinction of native or guest; registers would be based on current residence;
translations.idiomatic: Households would have no distinction of native or guest; registers would be based on current residence;

sentences.zh: 人無丁中，以貧富為差。

translations.literal: people would have no distinction of adult or minor; assessment would be by wealth and poverty.
translations.idiomatic: People would have no distinction of adult or minor; assessment would be by wealth and poverty.

sentences.zh: 不居處而行商者，在所州縣稅三十之一，度所取與居者均，使無僥利。

translations.literal: Merchants who did not reside locally but traveled in trade would be taxed one-thirtieth in the prefecture or county where they were; the amount taken would be balanced with that of residents, so there would be no advantage in evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants who did not reside locally but traveled in trade would be taxed one-thirtieth in the prefecture or county where they were. The amount taken would be balanced with that of residents, so there would be no advantage in evasion.

sentences.zh: 居人之稅，秋夏兩入之，俗有不便者三之。

translations.literal: Taxes on residents would be collected twice, in autumn and summer; where custom made this inconvenient, it could be divided into three payments.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes on residents would be collected twice, in autumn and summer. Where custom made this inconvenient, it could be divided into three payments.

sentences.zh: 其租、庸、雜徭悉省，而丁額不廢。

translations.literal: Rent, corvée, and miscellaneous labor levies would all be abolished, but the household quota would not be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Rent, corvée, and miscellaneous labor levies would all be abolished, but the household quota would not be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 其田畝之稅，率以大歷十四年墾田之數為準，而均收之。

translations.literal: The tax on fields would uniformly be assessed based on the amount of cultivated land in the fourteenth year of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: The tax on fields would uniformly be assessed based on the amount of cultivated land in the fourteenth year of Dali.

sentences.zh: 夏稅盡六月，秋稅盡十一月，歲終以戶賦增失進退長吏，而尚書度支總焉。

translations.literal: Summer tax would be completed by the sixth month, autumn tax by the eleventh month; at year's end increases or losses in household assessments would determine promotion or demotion of local officials, all overseen by the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax would be completed by the sixth month, autumn tax by the eleventh month. At year's end increases or losses in household assessments would determine promotion or demotion of local officials, all overseen by the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，使諭中外。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved it and ordered it announced within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it and ordered it announced within and without the court.

sentences.zh: 議者沮詰，以為租庸令行數百年，不可輕改。

translations.literal: Critics obstructed and challenged, arguing that the rent-and-corvée code had been in force for several hundred years and could not be lightly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Critics obstructed and challenged, arguing that the rent-and-corvée code had been in force for several hundred years and could not be lightly changed.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 天下果利之。

translations.literal: The empire indeed benefited from it.
translations.idiomatic: The empire indeed benefited from it.

sentences.zh: 自是人不土斷而地著，賦不加斂而增入，版籍不造而得其虛實，吏不誡而奸無所取，輕重之權始歸朝廷矣。

translations.literal: From then on people were not bound by native registration but settled where they lived; taxes were not increased yet revenue grew; registers were not newly made yet true conditions were known; officials needed no admonishment yet corruption had nothing to seize; the power to weigh light and heavy at last returned to the court.
translations.idiomatic: From then on people were not bound by native registration but settled where they lived. Taxes were not increased yet revenue grew. Registers were not newly made yet true conditions were known. Officials needed no admonishment yet corruption had nothing to seize. The power to weigh light and heavy at last returned to the court.

sentences.zh: 炎興嶺表，以單議悟天子，中外翕然屬望為賢相。

translations.literal: Yan rose from the southern frontier; with a single proposal he enlightened the Son of Heaven; within and without the court all united in looking to him as a worthy chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yan rose from the southern frontier. With a single proposal he enlightened the Son of Heaven, and within and without the court all united in looking to him as a worthy chief minister.

sentences.zh: 居數月，崔祐甫疾，不能事，喬琳免，炎獨當國，遂多變祐甫之政，減薄護元陵功優，人始不悅。

translations.literal: After several months, Cui Youfu fell ill and could not manage affairs; Qiao Lin was dismissed; Yan alone governed the state and then changed much of Youfu's policy, reducing and cutting the rewards for guarding Emperor Yuan's tomb; people began to be displeased.
translations.idiomatic: After several months, Cui Youfu fell ill and could not manage affairs. Qiao Lin was dismissed. Yan alone governed the state and then changed much of Youfu's policy, reducing and cutting the rewards for guarding Emperor Yuan's tomb. People began to be displeased.

sentences.zh: 又請開豐州陵陽渠，發畿縣民役作，閭裏騷然，渠卒不就。

translations.literal: He also requested opening the Lingyang Canal in Feng Prefecture, mobilizing the people of the capital districts for labor; neighborhoods were in uproar, and the canal was ultimately not completed.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested opening the Lingyang Canal in Feng Prefecture, mobilizing the people of the capital districts for labor. Neighborhoods were in uproar, and the canal was ultimately not completed.

sentences.zh: 素德元載，思有以報之，於是復議城原州，節度使段秀實謂「安邊卻敵，宜以緩計，方農事，不可遽興功。」

translations.literal: He had long been grateful to Yuan Zai and wished to repay him; therefore he again proposed fortifying Yuanzhou; Military Commissioner Duan Xiushi said: "Securing the border and repelling enemies should use gradual measures; farming is underway—it is not possible to hastily begin construction.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been grateful to Yuan Zai and wished to repay him. Therefore he again proposed fortifying Yuanzhou. Military Commissioner Duan Xiushi said: "Securing the border and repelling enemies should use gradual measures. Farming is underway—it is not possible to hastily begin construction.

sentences.zh: 炎怒，追秀實為司農卿，以邠寧李懷光督作，遣朱泚、崔寧統兵各萬人翼之。

translations.literal: Yan was enraged, recalled Xiushi as Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries, put Binning's Li Huai'guang in charge of construction, and dispatched Zhu Ci and Cui Ning each commanding ten thousand troops as wings.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was enraged, recalled Xiushi as director of the Court of Imperial Granaries, put Binning's Li Huai'guang in charge of construction, and dispatched Zhu Ci and Cui Ning each commanding ten thousand troops as wings.

sentences.zh: 詔書下，涇軍恚曰：「吾軍為國西屏十餘年。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, the Jing army angrily said: "Our army has served as the state's western shield for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, the Jing army angrily said: "Our army has served as the state's western shield for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 始自邠土，農桑地著之安，徙此榛莽中，手披足踐，既立城壘，則又投之塞外，且安寘此乎？」

translations.literal: We began from Bin lands, with the settled security of farming and sericulture; we were moved into this wilderness, clearing paths with our hands and feet; once we had built ramparts, we are now cast beyond the frontier—how can this be endured?
translations.idiomatic: We began from Bin lands, with the settled security of farming and sericulture. We were moved into this wilderness, clearing paths with our hands and feet. Once we had built ramparts, we are now cast beyond the frontier—how can this be endured?

sentences.zh: 又懷光持法嚴，舉軍畏之。

translations.literal: Moreover, Huai'guang enforced the law strictly, and the whole army feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Huai'guang enforced the law strictly, and the whole army feared him.

sentences.zh: 裨將劉文喜因人之怨，乃上疏求秀實、朱泚為使。

translations.literal: Lieutenant General Liu Wenxi, taking advantage of the men's resentment, submitted a memorial requesting Xiushi and Zhu Ci as commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant General Liu Wenxi, taking advantage of the men's resentment, submitted a memorial requesting Xiushi and Zhu Ci as commissioners.

sentences.zh: 詔以泚代懷光，文喜不奉詔，閉城拒守，質其子吐蕃以求援。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ci to replace Huai'guang; Wenxi did not obey the edict, closed the city and resisted, and sent his son as hostage to the Tibetans to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Ci to replace Huai'guang. Wenxi did not obey the edict, closed the city and resisted, and sent his son as hostage to the Tibetans to seek aid.

sentences.zh: 時方煬旱，人情騷攜，群臣皆請赦文喜，帝不聽。

translations.literal: At the time there was scorching drought and public unrest; all ministers requested pardon for Wenxi; the Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was scorching drought and public unrest. All ministers requested pardon for Wenxi. The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 詔減服禦給軍，且趣師涇州，士當受春服者皆即賜。

translations.literal: An edict reduced the Emperor's clothing allowance to supply the army and hastened troops to Jingzhou; soldiers due to receive spring uniforms were all immediately granted them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reduced the emperor's clothing allowance to supply the army and hastened troops to Jingzhou. Soldiers due to receive spring uniforms were all immediately granted them.

sentences.zh: 命泚、懷光率軍攻之，壘環其州。

translations.literal: Ci and Huai'guang were ordered to lead armies to attack; camps encircled the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ci and Huai'guang were ordered to lead armies to attack. Camps encircled the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 別將劉海賓斬文喜，獻其首，涇州平，而原卒不能城。

translations.literal: Separate commander Liu Haibin beheaded Wenxi and presented his head; Jingzhou was pacified, but in the end Yuanzhou could not be fortified.
translations.idiomatic: Separate commander Liu Haibin beheaded Wenxi and presented his head. Jingzhou was pacified, but in the end Yuanzhou could not be fortified.

sentences.zh: 又以劉晏劾載，已坐貶，乃出晏忠州，用庾準為荊南節度使，誣晏殺之，朝野側目。

translations.literal: Also, because Liu Yan had impeached Zai and had already been demoted for it, Yan was sent out to Zhongzhou; Yan Zhun was appointed Military Commissioner of Jingnan and falsely accused and killed Yan; court and populace looked on with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Also, because Liu Yan had impeached Zai and had already been demoted for it, Yan was sent out to Zhongzhou. Yan Zhun was appointed military commissioner of Jingnan and falsely accused and killed Yan. Court and populace looked on with alarm.

sentences.zh: 李正己表請晏罪，炎懼，乃遣腹心分走諸道：裴冀使東都、河陽、魏博，孫成使澤潞、礠邢、幽州，盧東美使河南、淄青，李舟使山南、湖南，王定使淮西。

translations.literal: Li Zhengji memorialized requesting Yan's crimes be investigated; Yan was afraid and therefore dispatched trusted agents separately to the various circuits: Pei Ji to the Eastern Capital, Heyang, and Weibo; Sun Cheng to Zelu, Cixing, and Youzhou; Lu Dongmei to Henan and Ziqing; Li Zhou to Shannan and Hunan; Wang Ding to Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji memorialized requesting Yan's crimes be investigated. Yan was afraid and therefore dispatched trusted agents separately to the various circuits: Pei Ji to the Eastern Capital, Heyang, and Weibo; Sun Cheng to Zelu, Cixing, and Youzhou; Lu Dongmei to Henan and Ziqing; Li Zhou to Shannan and Hunan; Wang Ding to Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 聲言宣慰，而實自辯解，言「晏往嘗傅會奸邪，謀立獨孤妃為後，帝自惡之，非它過也」。

translations.literal: They claimed to be on pacification missions but in fact were defending themselves, saying: "Yan in the past had attached himself to the wicked, plotting to make the Dugu consort empress—the Emperor himself detested this; there was no other offense."
translations.idiomatic: They claimed to be on pacification missions but in fact were defending themselves, saying: "Yan in the past had attached himself to the wicked, plotting to make the Dugu consort empress—the emperor himself detested this; there was no other offense."

sentences.zh: 帝聞，使中人復其言於正己，還報信然，於是帝意銜之，未發也。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this, he sent a palace envoy to repeat these words to Zhengji; the report returned confirming them; therefore the Emperor harbored resentment but did not yet act.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he sent a palace envoy to repeat these words to Zhengji. The report returned confirming them. Therefore the emperor harbored resentment but did not yet act.

sentences.zh: 會盧杞以門下侍郎同中書門下平章事，進炎中書侍郎，同秉政。

translations.literal: When Lu Qi was appointed Vice Director of the Gate and Co-Signatory Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat, Yan was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery, and both shared governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qi was appointed vice director of the Gate and co-signatory director of the Chancellery and Secretariat, Yan was promoted to vice director of the Chancellery, and both shared governance.

sentences.zh: 杞無術學，貌麽陋，炎薄之，托疾不與會食，杞陰為憾。

translations.literal: Qi had no learning or skill, and his appearance was small and ugly; Yan looked down on him, feigned illness and did not dine with him; Qi secretly resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had no learning or skill, and his appearance was small and ugly. Yan looked down on him, feigned illness and did not dine with him. Qi secretly resented this.

sentences.zh: 舊制，中書舍人分押尚書六曹，以平奏報。

translations.literal: Under the old system, secretariat draftsmen separately supervised the six bureaus of the Ministry and balanced memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, secretariat draftsmen separately supervised the six bureaus of the Ministry and balanced memorials and reports.

sentences.zh: 開元初，廢其職。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era, this duty was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan era, this duty was abolished.

sentences.zh: 杞請復之，炎固以為不可，杞益怒。

translations.literal: Qi requested its restoration; Yan firmly maintained it was impossible; Qi grew angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Qi requested its restoration. Yan firmly maintained it was impossible. Qi grew angrier.

sentences.zh: 又密啟主書過咎，逐之，炎曰：「主書，吾局吏也，吾當自治之，奈何相侵邪？」

translations.literal: Qi also secretly reported the chief clerk's faults and had him expelled; Yan said: "The chief clerk is an officer of my bureau; I should discipline him myself—why invade my authority?
translations.idiomatic: Qi also secretly reported the chief clerk's faults and had him expelled. Yan said: "The chief clerk is an officer of my bureau. I should discipline him myself—why invade my authority?

sentences.zh: 始，炎還朝，道襄、漢，因勸梁崇義入朝，後又使李舟邀說之，崇義益反側。

translations.literal: Initially, when Yan returned to court, passing through Xiang and Han, he urged Liang Chongyi to come to court; afterward he also sent Li Zhou to invite and persuade him; Chongyi grew ever more wavering and rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Yan returned to court, passing through Xiang and Han, he urged Liang Chongyi to come to court. Afterward he also sent Li Zhou to invite and persuade him. Chongyi grew ever more wavering and rebellious.

sentences.zh: 及其叛，議者歸咎炎，以為趣成之。

translations.literal: When he rebelled, critics blamed Yan, believing he had hastened it.
translations.idiomatic: When he rebelled, critics blamed Yan, believing he had hastened it.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以淮西李希烈統諸軍致討，炎曰：「希烈始與李忠臣為子，逐忠臣取其位，此可以任乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to put Huaixi's Li Xilie in command of the armies for the punitive campaign; Yan said: "Xilie first became Li Zhongchen's adopted son, then drove Zhongchen out and took his position—can such a man be entrusted?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to put Huaixi's Li Xilie in command of the armies for the punitive campaign. Yan said: "Xilie first became Li Zhongchen's adopted son, then drove Zhongchen out and took his position—can such a man be entrusted?

sentences.zh: 居無尺寸功，猶倔強不奉法，設使平賊，陛下將何以制之？」

translations.literal: He has achieved not the slightest merit, yet remains stubborn and disobedient to law; suppose he pacifies the rebels—how will Your Majesty control him?
translations.idiomatic: He has achieved not the slightest merit, yet remains stubborn and disobedient to law. Suppose he pacifies the rebels—how will Your Majesty control him?

sentences.zh: 帝不能平，恚曰：「氍不能食吾言。」

translations.literal: The Emperor could not be appeased and angrily said: "This wool rug cannot digest my words."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not be appeased and angrily said: "This wool rug cannot digest my words."

sentences.zh: 遂用希烈。

translations.literal: Xilie was therefore employed.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was therefore employed.

sentences.zh: 又嘗訪群臣可大任者，杞薦張鎰、嚴郢，而炎舉崔昭、趙惠伯。

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked the ministers who could bear great responsibility; Qi recommended Zhang Yi and Yan Yi, while Yan recommended Cui Zhao and Zhao Huibo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked the ministers who could bear great responsibility. Qi recommended Zhang Yi and Yan Yi, while Yan recommended Cui Zhao and Zhao Huibo.

sentences.zh: 帝以炎論議疏闊，遂罷為尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered Yan's policy discussions loose and broad, and therefore dismissed him to Left Vice Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered Yan's policy discussions loose and broad, and therefore dismissed him to left vice director of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 既謝，對延英訖，不至中書，杞怒，益欲中之。

translations.literal: After his audience of thanks, having answered at the Yanying Hall, he did not go to the Chancellery; Qi was enraged and wished even more to strike at him.
translations.idiomatic: After his audience of thanks, having answered at the Yanying Hall, he did not go to the Chancellery. Qi was enraged and wished even more to strike at him.

sentences.zh: 先是，嚴郢為京兆尹，不附炎，炎諷御史張著劾之，罷兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Previously, Yan Yi served as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and did not attach himself to Yan; Yan prompted Censor Zhang Zhu to impeach him, and he was dismissed from his concurrent post as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Yan Yi served as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and did not attach himself to Yan. Yan prompted Censor Zhang Zhu to impeach him, and he was dismissed from his concurrent post as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 源休與郢不善，自流人擢休為京兆少尹，令伺郢過。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu was on bad terms with Yi; from exile Xiu was promoted to Vice Governor of Jingzhao and ordered to watch for Yi's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu was on bad terms with Yi. From exile Xiu was promoted to vice governor of Jingzhao and ordered to watch for Yi's faults.

sentences.zh: 休反與郢善，炎怒。

translations.literal: Xiu instead became friendly with Yi; Yan was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu instead became friendly with Yi. Yan was enraged.

sentences.zh: 會張光晟謀殺回紇酋帥，乃使休使回紇。

translations.literal: When Zhang Guangchen plotted to kill the Uyghur chieftain, Xiu was sent as envoy to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Guangchen plotted to kill the Uyghur chieftain, Xiu was sent as envoy to the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 郢坐度田不實，下除大理卿。

translations.literal: Yi was implicated for false land surveys and demoted to Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was implicated for false land surveys and demoted to director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 至是炎罷，其子弘業賕賂狼藉，故杞引郢為御史大夫按之，並得它過。

translations.literal: At this time when Yan was dismissed, his son Hongye's bribes were exposed in disarray; therefore Qi brought in Yi as Censor-in-Chief to investigate, and other offenses were also found.
translations.idiomatic: At this time when Yan was dismissed, his son Hongye's bribes were exposed in disarray. Therefore Qi brought in Yi as censor-in-chief to investigate, and other offenses were also found.

sentences.zh: 惠伯為河南尹時，嘗市炎第為官廨。

translations.literal: When Huibo was Metropolitan Governor of Henan, he had once purchased Yan's mansion for government offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Huibo was metropolitan governor of Henan, he had once purchased Yan's mansion for government offices.

sentences.zh: 御史劾炎宰相抑吏市私第，貴取其直。

translations.literal: Censors impeached Yan for, as chief minister, coercing an official to buy his private mansion at an inflated price.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached Yan for, as chief minister, coercing an official to buy his private mansion at an inflated price.

sentences.zh: 杞召大理正田晉評罪，晉曰：「宰相於庶官比監臨，計羨利，罪奪官。」

translations.literal: Qi summoned Court of Judicial Review Director Tian Jin to assess the crime; Jin said: "A chief minister toward a subordinate official is like a supervisor; calculating excess profit, the penalty is deprivation of office.
translations.idiomatic: Qi summoned Court of Judicial Review director Tian Jin to assess the crime. Jin said: "A chief minister toward a subordinate official is like a supervisor. Calculating excess profit, the penalty is deprivation of office.

sentences.zh: 杞怒，謫晉衡州司馬。

translations.literal: Qi was enraged and demoted Jin to Military Staff Officer of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was enraged and demoted Jin to military staff officer of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是當監主自盜，罪絞。

translations.literal: Thereupon the crime of a supervisor stealing from himself was assessed as strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the crime of a supervisor stealing from himself was assessed as strangulation.

sentences.zh: 開元時，蕭嵩嘗度曲江南，欲立私廟，以為天子臨幸處乃止，後炎復取以立廟。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, Xiao Song once surveyed land south of the bend of the river and wished to build a private temple; he stopped because it was where the Son of Heaven would visit; later Yan again took it to build a temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era, Xiao Song once surveyed land south of the bend of the river and wished to build a private temple. He stopped because it was where the Son of Heaven would visit. Later Yan again took it to build a temple.

sentences.zh: 飛語云：「地有王氣，故炎取之。」

translations.literal: Slander said: "The land had royal qi, and therefore Yan took it.
translations.idiomatic: Slander said: "The land had royal qi, and therefore Yan took it.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，震怒，會獄具，詔三司同覆，貶崖州司馬同正。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this, he was shaken with rage; when the case was complete, an edict ordered the Three Offices to review jointly; Yan was demoted to Acting Military Staff Officer of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he was shaken with rage. When the case was complete, an edict ordered the Three Offices to review jointly. Yan was demoted to acting military staff officer of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 未至百里，賜死，年五十五。

translations.literal: Before he had gone a hundred li, death was granted; he was fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had gone a hundred li, death was granted. He was fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 貶惠伯多田尉，亦殺之。

translations.literal: Huibo was demoted to Captain of Duotian and also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huibo was demoted to captain of Duotian and also killed.

sentences.zh: 初，炎矯飭誌節，頗得名。

translations.literal: Initially, Yan cultivated an austere integrity and gained considerable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Yan cultivated an austere integrity and gained considerable reputation.

sentences.zh: 既傅會元載抵罪，俄而得政，然忮害根中，不能自止。

translations.literal: After attaching himself to Yuan Zai and sharing his guilt, he soon obtained power, yet malice was rooted within him and he could not stop himself.
translations.idiomatic: After attaching himself to Yuan Zai and sharing his guilt, he soon obtained power, yet malice was rooted within him and he could not stop himself.

sentences.zh: 眥睚必讎，果於用私，終以此及禍。

translations.literal: He always avenged the smallest grudge, was decisive in using private means, and ultimately met disaster through this.
translations.idiomatic: He always avenged the smallest grudge, was decisive in using private means, and ultimately met disaster through this.

sentences.zh: 自道州還也，家人以綠袍木簡棄之，炎止曰：「吾嶺上一逐吏，超登上臺，可常哉？

translations.literal: When he returned from Daozhou, his family discarded his green robe and wooden tally; Yan stopped them, saying: "I was an exiled official on the southern frontier who leaped to the highest platform—can this be permanent?
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from Daozhou, his family discarded his green robe and wooden tally. Yan stopped them, saying: "I was an exiled official on the southern frontier who leaped to the highest platform—can this be permanent?

sentences.zh: 且有非常之福，必有非常之禍，安可棄是乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, where there is extraordinary fortune, there must be extraordinary calamity—how can these be discarded?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, where there is extraordinary fortune, there must be extraordinary calamity—how can these be discarded?

sentences.zh: 及貶，還所服。

translations.literal: When he was demoted, he put them on again.
translations.idiomatic: When he was demoted, he put them on again.

sentences.zh: 久之，詔復其官，謚肅湣，左丞孔戣駁之，更曰平厲。

translations.literal: After a long time, an edict restored his office; his posthumous title was Su Min; Left Vice Director Kong Rui rejected it, and it was changed to Ping Li.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, an edict restored his office. His posthumous title was Su Min. Left Vice Director Kong Rui rejected it, and it was changed to Ping Li.

sentences.zh: 庾準者，常州人。

translations.literal: Yan Zhun was a native of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhun was a native of Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 無學術，以柔媚自進，得幸於王縉，驟至中書舍人，時流嗤薄之。

translations.literal: He had no learning; through soft flattery he advanced himself, gained favor with Wang Jin, and rapidly reached Secretariat Draftsman; contemporaries scorned and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: He had no learning. Through soft flattery he advanced himself, gained favor with Wang Jin, and rapidly reached secretariat draftsman. Contemporaries scorned and despised him.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was twice transferred to Right Vice Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice transferred to right vice director of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 縉得罪，出為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jin fell from grace, Zhun was sent out as Prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell from grace, Zhun was sent out as prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 復入為司農卿。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as director of the Court of Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 又善炎，故炎使節度荊南；

translations.literal: He was also on good terms with Yan; therefore Yan had him made Military Commissioner of Jingnan;
translations.idiomatic: He was also on good terms with Yan. Therefore Yan had him made military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 晏已誣死，引為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: after Yan was falsely killed, he was brought in as Left Vice Director of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan was falsely killed, he was brought in as left vice director of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 建中三年卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Jianzhong and was posthumously granted Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Jianzhong and was posthumously granted minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 嚴郢，字叔敖，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Yan Yi, styled Shu'ao, was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yi, courtesy name Shu'ao, came from Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父正誨，以才吏更七郡、終江南西道采訪使。

translations.literal: His father Zhenghui was a talented clerk who served in seven prefectures and ended as Regional Inspector of Jiangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhenghui was a talented clerk who served in seven prefectures and ended as regional inspector of Jiangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 郢及進士第，補太常協律郎，守東都太廟。

translations.literal: Yi passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Harmonizing Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and guarded the Eastern Capital Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Yi passed the jinshi examination, was appointed harmonizing director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and guarded the Eastern Capital Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，郢取神主秘於家，至德初，定洛陽，有司得以奉迎還廟，擢大理司直。

translations.literal: During the Lushan rebellion, Yi secretly kept the spirit tablets at home; in the early Zhide era, when Luoyang was secured, the responsible offices were able to receive and return them to the temple; he was promoted to Directing Censor in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: During the Lushan rebellion, Yi secretly kept the spirit tablets at home. In the early Zhide era, when Luoyang was secured, the responsible offices were able to receive and return them to the temple. He was promoted to directing censor in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 呂諲鎮江陵，表為判官。

translations.literal: When Lü Jin governed Jiangling, he memorialized for Yi as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Jin governed Jiangling, he memorialized for Yi as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 方士申泰芝以術得幸肅宗，遨遊湖、衡間，以妖幻詭眾，奸贓鉅萬，潭州刺史龐承鼎按治。

translations.literal: The adept Shen Taizhi gained favor with Emperor Suzong through his arts, wandered between the lakes and Heng mountains, deceived the masses with sorcery and illusion, and amassed bribes worth millions; Tan Prefect Pang Chengding investigated and prosecuted him.
translations.idiomatic: The adept Shen Taizhi gained favor with Emperor Suzong through his arts, wandered between the lakes and Heng mountains, deceived the masses with sorcery and illusion, and amassed bribes worth millions. Tan Prefect Pang Chengding investigated and prosecuted him.

sentences.zh: 帝不信，召還泰芝，下承鼎江陵獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not believe it, recalled Taizhi, and imprisoned Chengding in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not believe it, recalled Taizhi, and imprisoned Chengding in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 郢具言泰芝左道，帝遣中人與諲雜訊有狀，帝不為然。

translations.literal: Yi fully explained Taizhi's heterodox ways; the Emperor sent a palace envoy with Jin to interrogate jointly, and evidence was found; the Emperor was not persuaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yi fully explained Taizhi's heterodox ways. The emperor sent a palace envoy with Jin to interrogate jointly, and evidence was found. The emperor was not persuaded.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞敬羽白貸泰芝，郢方入朝，亟辨之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Jing Yu petitioned to pardon Taizhi; Yi had just entered court and urgently argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Jing Yu petitioned to pardon Taizhi. Yi had just entered court and urgently argued against it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，叱郢去。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and shouted at Yi to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and shouted at Yi to leave.

sentences.zh: 郢復曰：「承鼎劾泰芝詭沓有實，泰芝言承鼎驗左不存。

translations.literal: Yi replied again: "Chengding's impeachment of Taizhi for deception and evasion has substance; Taizhi says Chengding's evidence of guilt does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied again: "Chengding's impeachment of Taizhi for deception and evasion has substance. Taizhi says Chengding's evidence of guilt does not exist.

sentences.zh: 今緩有罪，急無罪，臣死不敢如詔。」

translations.literal: Now to be lenient toward the guilty and urgent toward the innocent—I would die rather than obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Now to be lenient toward the guilty and urgent toward the innocent—I would die rather than obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝卒殺承鼎，流郢建州。

translations.literal: The Emperor ultimately executed Chengding and exiled Yi to Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately executed Chengding and exiled Yi to Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泰芝後坐妖妄不道誅。

translations.literal: Taizhi was later executed for sorcery, delusion, and immoral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhi was later executed for sorcery, delusion, and immoral conduct.

sentences.zh: 代宗初，追還承鼎官，召郢為監察御史，連署帥府司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Daizong's reign, Chengding's office was posthumously restored; Yi was summoned as Investigating Censor and concurrently served as Military Staff Officer in a commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Daizong's reign, Chengding's office was posthumously restored. Yi was summoned as investigating censor and concurrently served as military staff officer in a commander's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀表為關內、河東副元帥府判官，遷行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi memorialized for him as administrative aide in the Guannei and Hedong Deputy Commander-in-Chief's headquarters; he was transferred to Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi memorialized for him as administrative aide in the Guannei and Hedong Deputy Commander-in-Chief's headquarters. He was transferred to chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 子儀鎮邠州，檄郢主留務。

translations.literal: When Ziyi governed Bin Prefecture, he ordered Yi to manage remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi governed Bin Prefecture, he ordered Yi to manage remaining affairs.

sentences.zh: 河中士卒不樂戍邠，多逃還。

translations.literal: Soldiers of Hezhong did not wish to garrison Bin and many fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers of Hezhong did not wish to garrison Bin and many fled back.

sentences.zh: 郢取渠首屍之，乃定。

translations.literal: Yi took the ringleaders and displayed their corpses; order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took the ringleaders and displayed their corpses. Order was restored.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，召至京師，元載薦之帝，時載得罪，不見用。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was summoned to the capital; Yuan Zai recommended him to the Emperor, but at the time Zai had fallen from grace and Yi was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, he was summoned to the capital. Yuan Zai recommended him to the emperor, but at the time Zai had fallen from grace and Yi was not employed.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李棲筠亦薦郢，帝曰：「是元載所厚，可乎？」

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Qiyun also recommended Yi; the Emperor said: "This is one whom Yuan Zai favored heavily—is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Li Qiyun also recommended Yi. The emperor said: "This is one whom Yuan Zai favored heavily—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「如郢材力，陛下不自取，而留為奸人用邪？」

translations.literal: The reply was: "With Yi's talent and ability, if Your Majesty does not take him for yourself, will you leave him for wicked men to use?"
translations.idiomatic: The reply was: "With Yi's talent and ability, if Your Majesty does not take him for yourself, will you leave him for wicked men to use?"

sentences.zh: 即日拜河南尹、水陸運使。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed Metropolitan Governor of Henan and Commissioner of Water and Land Transport.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was appointed metropolitan governor of Henan and commissioner of water and land transport.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，進拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali, he was promoted to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Dali, he was promoted to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 嚴明持法令，疾惡撫窮，敢誅殺，盜賊一衰，減隸官匠丁數百千人，號稱職尹。

translations.literal: Strict and clear in upholding laws, hating evil and comforting the poor, daring to execute and kill, he caused bandits and thieves to decline; he reduced official artisan corvée laborers by several hundred or thousand men, and was called a worthy governor.
translations.idiomatic: Strict and clear in upholding laws, hating evil and comforting the poor, daring to execute and kill, he caused bandits and thieves to decline. He reduced official artisan corvée laborers by several hundred or thousand men and was called a worthy governor.

sentences.zh: 宰相楊炎請屯田豐州，發關輔民鑿陵陽渠，郢習朔邊病利，即奏：「舊屯肥饒地，今十不墾一，水田甚廣，力不及而廢。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yang Yan requested garrison farming in Feng Prefecture and mobilizing Guanfu people to dig the Lingyang Canal; Yi, familiar with the frontier's hardships and benefits, immediately memorialized: "Old garrison lands were fertile and rich; now not one in ten is cultivated; paddy fields are very extensive but abandoned for lack of labor.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yang Yan requested garrison farming in Feng Prefecture and mobilizing Guanfu people to dig the Lingyang Canal. Yi, familiar with the frontier's hardships and benefits, immediately memorialized: "Old garrison lands were fertile and rich. Now not one in ten is cultivated. Paddy fields are very extensive but abandoned for lack of labor.

sentences.zh: 若發二京關輔民浚豐渠營田，擾而無利。

translations.literal: If people of the Two Capitals and Guanfu are mobilized to dredge the Feng Canal and open fields, there will be disturbance without profit.
translations.idiomatic: If people of the Two Capitals and Guanfu are mobilized to dredge the Feng Canal and open fields, there will be disturbance without profit.

sentences.zh: 請以內苑蒔稻驗之，秦地膏腴，田上上，耕者皆畿人，月一代，功甚易，又人給錢月八千，糧不在，然有司常募不能足。

translations.literal: I request testing this by planting rice in the inner park; Qin lands are rich and fertile, fields of the highest grade; all cultivators are capital district people, rotating monthly, the work very easy; moreover each person is paid eight thousand cash monthly, with no grain provided—yet responsible offices often cannot fill recruitment quotas.
translations.idiomatic: I request testing this by planting rice in the inner park. Qin lands are rich and fertile, fields of the highest grade. All cultivators are capital district people, rotating monthly—the work is very easy. Moreover each person is paid eight thousand cash monthly with no grain provided, yet responsible offices often cannot fill recruitment quotas.

sentences.zh: 合府縣共之，計一農歲錢九萬六千，米月七斛二斗，大抵歲僦丁三百，錢二千八百八十萬，米二千一百六十斛，臣恐終歲獲不酬費。

translations.literal: Combining prefectures and counties, one farmer costs ninety-six thousand cash per year and seven hu two dou of rice monthly; roughly hiring three hundred laborers yearly costs twenty-eight million eight hundred thousand cash and two thousand one hundred sixty hu of rice—I fear the year's harvest will not repay the expense.
translations.idiomatic: Combining prefectures and counties, one farmer costs ninety-six thousand cash per year and seven hu two dou of rice monthly. Roughly hiring three hundred laborers yearly costs twenty-eight million eight hundred thousand cash and two thousand one hundred sixty hu of rice. I fear the year's harvest will not repay the expense.

sentences.zh: 況二千里發人出塞，而歲一代乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, to mobilize people two thousand li beyond the frontier with yearly rotation?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to mobilize people two thousand li beyond the frontier with yearly rotation?

sentences.zh: 又自太原轉糧以哺，私出資費倍之，是虛畿甸，事空徭也。」

translations.literal: Also transporting grain from Taiyuan to feed them, with private expenses doubling the cost—this empties the capital districts for a futile corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Also transporting grain from Taiyuan to feed them, with private expenses doubling the cost—this empties the capital districts for a futile corvée.

sentences.zh: 郢又言：「五城舊屯地至廣，請以鑿渠糧俾諸城，夏貸冬輸，取渠工布帛給田者，令據直轉谷，則關輔免調發，而諸城辟田。」

translations.literal: Yi also said: "The old garrison lands of the five cities are extremely vast; I request allocating canal-digging grain to the various cities, lending in summer and repaying in winter, taking cloth and silk from canal labor to give to farmers, letting them convert at fair value to grain—then Guanfu would be spared mobilization and the various cities would open fields."
translations.idiomatic: Yi also said: "The old garrison lands of the five cities are extremely vast. I request allocating canal-digging grain to the various cities, lending in summer and repaying in winter, taking cloth and silk from canal labor to give to farmers, letting them convert at fair value to grain—then Guanfu would be spared mobilization and the various cities would open fields."

sentences.zh: 炎不許，渠卒不成，棄之。

translations.literal: Yan did not agree; the canal was ultimately not completed and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yan did not agree. The canal was ultimately not completed and abandoned.

sentences.zh: 御史臺請天下斷獄一切待報，唯殺人許償死，論徒者得悉徙邊。

translations.literal: The Censorate requested that all criminal judgments throughout the empire await imperial report; only for murder would compensation for life be permitted; all sentenced to penal servitude would be entirely exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate requested that all criminal judgments throughout the empire await imperial report. Only for murder would compensation for life be permitted. All sentenced to penal servitude would be entirely exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 郢言：「罪人徙邊，即流也。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Exiling criminals to the frontier is banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: "Exiling criminals to the frontier is banishment.

sentences.zh: 流有三，而一用之，誠難。

translations.literal: Banishment has three grades, yet using only one is truly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Banishment has three grades, yet using only one is truly difficult.

sentences.zh: 且殺人外猶有十惡、偽造用符印、強光火諸盜，今一徙之，法太輕，不足禁惡。

translations.literal: Moreover, apart from murder there are still the Ten Abominations, counterfeiting seals and documents, armed robbery, arson, and various thefts; to exile all alike makes the law too light and insufficient to restrain evil.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, apart from murder there are still the Ten Abominations, counterfeiting seals and documents, armed robbery, arson, and various thefts. To exile all alike makes the law too light and insufficient to restrain evil.

sentences.zh: 又罪抵徒，科別差殊，或毆傷、夫婦離非義絕、養男別姓、立嫡不如式、私度關、冒戶等不可悉，而與十惡同徙，即輕重不倫。

translations.literal: Also, crimes meriting penal servitude differ in category and degree—such as assault, improper divorce without statutory severance, adopting a son of another surname, establishing an heir not according to form, crossing borders privately, false household registration, and others too numerous to list—yet to exile them together with the Ten Abominations makes light and heavy unequal.
translations.idiomatic: Also, crimes meriting penal servitude differ in category and degree—such as assault, improper divorce without statutory severance, adopting a son of another surname, establishing an heir not according to form, crossing borders privately, false household registration, and others too numerous to list. To exile them together with the Ten Abominations makes light and heavy unequal.

sentences.zh: 又按，京師天下聚，論徒者至廣，例不覆讞，今若悉待報，有司斷決有程，月不啻五千獄，正恐牒按填委，章程紊撓。

translations.literal: Moreover, the capital gathers people from all the empire; those sentenced to penal servitude are extremely numerous and by precedent are not reviewed; if all now await report, responsible offices have fixed schedules for judgments—no less than five thousand cases monthly—I fear documents and records will pile up and regulations will be thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the capital gathers people from all the empire. Those sentenced to penal servitude are extremely numerous and by precedent are not reviewed. If all now await report, responsible offices have fixed schedules for judgments—no less than five thousand cases monthly. I fear documents and records will pile up and regulations will be thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 且邊及近邊犯死徒流者，若何為差？

translations.literal: Moreover, for those on the frontier and near the frontier who merit death, penal servitude, or banishment—how should distinctions be made?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for those on the frontier and near the frontier who merit death, penal servitude, or banishment—how should distinctions be made?

sentences.zh: 請下有司更議。」

translations.literal: I request that responsible offices be ordered to reconsider.
translations.idiomatic: I request that responsible offices be ordered to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 炎惡異己，陰諷御史張著劾郢匿發民浚渠，使怨歸上。

translations.literal: Yan hated those who differed from him and secretly prompted Censor Zhang Zhu to impeach Yi for concealing the mobilization of people to dredge canals, so that resentment would fall on the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yan hated those who differed from him and secretly prompted Censor Zhang Zhu to impeach Yi for concealing the mobilization of people to dredge canals, so that resentment would fall on the emperor.

sentences.zh: 系金吾。

translations.literal: Yi was imprisoned by the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was imprisoned by the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 長安中日數千人遮建福門訟郢冤，帝微知之，削兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In Chang'an, several thousand people daily blocked Jianfu Gate to petition Yi's injustice; the Emperor slightly understood and stripped him of his concurrent post as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an, several thousand people daily blocked Jianfu Gate to petition Yi's injustice. The emperor slightly understood and stripped him of his concurrent post as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 人知郢得原，皆迎拜。

translations.literal: When people knew Yi had been pardoned, all came out to welcome and bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: When people knew Yi had been pardoned, all came out to welcome and bow to him.

sentences.zh: 會秋旱，郢請蠲租稅，炎令度支御史按覆，以不實，罷為大理卿。

translations.literal: When autumn drought occurred, Yi requested remission of rents and taxes; Yan ordered revenue censors to investigate and review; finding it untrue, Yi was dismissed to Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn drought occurred, Yi requested remission of rents and taxes. Yan ordered revenue censors to investigate and review. Finding it untrue, Yi was dismissed to director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 炎之罷，盧杞引郢為御史大夫，共謀炎罪。

translations.literal: When Yan was dismissed, Lu Qi brought in Yi as Censor-in-Chief to jointly plot Yan's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was dismissed, Lu Qi brought in Yi as censor-in-chief to jointly plot Yan's crimes.

sentences.zh: 即逮捕河中觀察使趙惠伯下獄，楚掠慘棘，鍛成其罪，卒逐炎崖州，惠伯費州。

translations.literal: They immediately arrested Hedong Regional Inspector Zhao Huibo and imprisoned him; torture was cruel and severe, crimes were fabricated, and ultimately Yan was exiled to Yazhou and Huibo to Feizhou.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately arrested Hedong regional inspector Zhao Huibo and imprisoned him. Torture was cruel and severe, crimes were fabricated, and ultimately Yan was exiled to Yazhou and Huibo to Feizhou.

sentences.zh: 天下以郢挾宰相報仇為不直。

translations.literal: The empire considered Yi, wielding the chief minister's power for revenge, unjust.
translations.idiomatic: The empire considered Yi, wielding the chief minister's power for revenge, unjust.

sentences.zh: 然杞用郢敗炎，內忌郢才，因按蔡廷玉事，殺御史鄭詹，出郢為費州刺史。

translations.literal: Yet Qi used Yi to defeat Yan, inwardly envied Yi's talent, and through investigating the Cai Tingyu affair, killed Censor Zheng Zhan and sent Yi out as Prefect of Feizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qi used Yi to defeat Yan, inwardly envied Yi's talent, and through investigating the Cai Tingyu affair, killed Censor Zheng Zhan and sent Yi out as prefect of Feizhou.

sentences.zh: 道逢柩殯，問之，或曰：「趙惠伯之殯。」

translations.literal: On the road he encountered a funeral procession; asking about it, someone said: "It is Zhao Huibo's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he encountered a funeral procession. Asking about it, someone said: "It is Zhao Huibo's funeral.

sentences.zh: 郢內慚，忽忽歲餘卒。

translations.literal: Yi was inwardly ashamed; after more than a year in despondency he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was inwardly ashamed. After more than a year in despondency he died.

sentences.zh: 竇參，字時中，刑部尚書誕四世孫。

translations.literal: Dou Can, styled Shizhong, was the fourth-generation descendant of Minister of Justice Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can, courtesy name Shizhong, was the fourth-generation descendant of Minister of Justice Dan.

sentences.zh: 學律令，為人矜嚴悻直，果於斷。

translations.literal: He studied laws and statutes; by nature he was stern, upright, and obstinate, decisive in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He studied laws and statutes. By nature he was stern, upright, and obstinate, decisive in judgment.

sentences.zh: 以蔭累為萬年尉。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he cumulatively became Assistant Magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he cumulatively became assistant magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 同舍當夕直者，聞親疾惶遽，參為代之。

translations.literal: A colleague due for night duty heard of a parent's illness and rushed off in panic; Can substituted for him.
translations.idiomatic: A colleague due for night duty heard of a parent's illness and rushed off in panic. Can substituted for him.

sentences.zh: 會失囚，京兆按直簿劾其人，參曰：「彼以不及謁而往，參當坐。」

translations.literal: A prisoner escaped; the Metropolitan Governor checked the duty roster and impeached that man; Can said: "He went because he had no time to request leave—I should bear the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: A prisoner escaped. The metropolitan governor checked the duty roster and impeached that man. Can said: "He went because he had no time to request leave—I should bear the punishment.

sentences.zh: 乃貶江夏尉，人皆義之。

translations.literal: He was therefore demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Jiangxia; all considered him righteous.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore demoted to assistant magistrate of Jiangxia. All considered him righteous.

sentences.zh: 遷奉先尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Fengxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Fengxian.

sentences.zh: 男子曹芬兄弟隸北軍，醉暴其妹，父救不止，恚赴井死。

translations.literal: A man named Cao Fen and his brothers, attached to the Northern Army, drunkenly violated their sister; their father tried to stop them but could not, and in rage threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Cao Fen and his brothers, attached to the Northern Army, drunkenly violated their sister. Their father tried to stop them but could not, and in rage threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 參當兄弟重辟，眾請俟免喪，參曰：「父繇子死，若以喪延，是殺父不坐。」

translations.literal: Can assessed the brothers the death penalty; the crowd requested waiting until mourning ended; Can said: "The father died because of the sons—if delayed for mourning, it means killing one's father goes unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Can assessed the brothers the death penalty. The crowd requested waiting until mourning ended. Can said: "The father died because of the sons—if delayed for mourning, it means killing one's father goes unpunished.

sentences.zh: 皆榜殺之，一縣畏伏。

translations.literal: All were beaten and executed; the whole county feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: All were beaten and executed. The whole county feared and submitted.

sentences.zh: 進大理司直，按江淮獄揚州，節度使陳少遊偃蹇不郊迎，遣軍吏致問，參厲辭譙讓，少遊慚，往謁參，參不顧即去。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Directing Censor in the Court of Judicial Review and investigated cases in Huai and Jiang at Yangzhou; Military Commissioner Chen Shaoyou was arrogant and did not come out to the suburbs to welcome him, sending a military officer to inquire; Can spoke sharply and reproached him; Shaoyou was ashamed and went to visit Can, but Can paid no attention and left immediately.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to directing censor in the Court of Judicial Review and investigated cases in Huai and Jiang at Yangzhou. Military Commissioner Chen Shaoyou was arrogant and did not come out to the suburbs to welcome him, sending a military officer to inquire. Can spoke sharply and reproached him. Shaoyou was ashamed and went to visit Can, but Can paid no attention and left immediately.

sentences.zh: 婺州刺史鄧珽盜贓八千緡，宰相右珽，欲免輸其財，詔百官集尚書省議，多希意為助，參獨持法，卒輸入之。

translations.literal: Wu Prefect Deng Ting embezzled eight thousand strings; the chief minister favored Ting and wished to exempt him from paying the money; an edict ordered all officials to gather at the Ministry for discussion; most curried favor to help; Can alone upheld the law, and ultimately the money was paid in.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Prefect Deng Ting embezzled eight thousand strings. The chief minister favored Ting and wished to exempt him from paying the money. An edict ordered all officials to gather at the Ministry for discussion. Most curried favor to help. Can alone upheld the law, and ultimately the money was paid in.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 湖南判官馬彜發部令贓千萬，令之子因權幸誣奏彜，參往按，直其侵蔑。

translations.literal: Hunan Administrative Aide Ma Yi exposed a prefect's embezzlement of ten million; the prefect's son, through powerful favorites, falsely impeached Yi; Can went to investigate and vindicated the slander.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan administrative aide Ma Yi exposed a prefect's embezzlement of ten million. The prefect's son, through powerful favorites, falsely impeached Yi. Can went to investigate and vindicated the slander.

sentences.zh: 彜後佐曹王臯，以幹直聞者也。

translations.literal: Yi later served Prince Cao Li Gao and was known for capability and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yi later served Prince Cao Li Gao and was known for capability and integrity.

sentences.zh: 入為御史中丞，舉劾無所回忌。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Censor-in-Chief, impeaching without hesitation or fear.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as censor-in-chief, impeaching without hesitation or fear.

sentences.zh: 德宗數召見，語天下事，或決大議，帝器之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong repeatedly summoned him, discussed affairs of the empire, and sometimes decided great matters; the Emperor valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong repeatedly summoned him, discussed affairs of the empire, and sometimes decided great matters. The emperor valued him.

sentences.zh: 然多與宰相駁異，數為排卻，卒無以傷。

translations.literal: Yet he often differed from the chief ministers and was repeatedly pushed aside, yet in the end they could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he often differed from the chief ministers and was repeatedly pushed aside, yet in the end they could not harm him.

sentences.zh: 參由是無所憚，或率情制事矣。

translations.literal: Can therefore feared nothing and sometimes governed affairs according to personal inclination.
translations.idiomatic: Can therefore feared nothing and sometimes governed affairs according to personal inclination.

sentences.zh: 時定百官班稟，參嘗為大理司直，故多其入，使在丞上。

translations.literal: When official ranks and salaries were fixed, Can had once been Directing Censor in the Court of Judicial Review, and therefore his income was increased, placing him above the directors.
translations.idiomatic: When official ranks and salaries were fixed, Can had once been directing censor in the Court of Judicial Review, and therefore his income was increased, placing him above the directors.

sentences.zh: 惡詹事李昇，抑其班在諸府少尹下。

translations.literal: He hated Mentor of the Heir Apparent Li Sheng and suppressed his rank below the vice governors of various offices.
translations.idiomatic: He hated mentor of the heir apparent Li Sheng and suppressed his rank below the vice governors of various offices.

sentences.zh: 中外稍惡其專。

translations.literal: Within and without the court, people gradually disliked his arbitrariness.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the court, people gradually disliked his arbitrariness.

sentences.zh: 進兼戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to concurrently serve as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrently serve as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 民家生豕二首四足，有司欲以聞，參曰：「此乃豕禍。」

translations.literal: A commoner's household bore a pig with two heads and four legs; responsible offices wished to report it; Can said: "This is a pig calamity.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner's household bore a pig with two heads and four legs. Responsible offices wished to report it. Can said: "This is a pig calamity.

sentences.zh: 屏不奏。

translations.literal: He suppressed it and did not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed it and did not memorialize.

sentences.zh: 陳少遊死，子請襲封，參大署省門曰：「少遊位將相，以艱危易節，上含垢不忍發，其息容得傳襲邪？」

translations.literal: When Chen Shaoyou died, his son requested inherited enfeoffment; Can wrote large characters on the ministry gate: "Shaoyou held the rank of general and minister, yet changed his loyalty in peril—the Emperor swallowed the offense and would not expose it; can his son be allowed to inherit the title?
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shaoyou died, his son requested inherited enfeoffment. Can wrote large characters on the ministry gate: "Shaoyou held the rank of general and minister, yet changed his loyalty in peril—the emperor swallowed the offense and would not expose it. Can his son be allowed to inherit the title?

sentences.zh: 神策將軍孟華戰有功，或誣以反，龍武將軍李建玉陷吐蕃自拔歸，部曲告與虜通，皆論死。

translations.literal: Shence General Meng Hua had merit in battle but was falsely accused of rebellion; Longwu General Li Jianyu, having escaped from the Tibetans and returned, was reported by his troops as communicating with the enemy—all were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shence General Meng Hua had merit in battle but was falsely accused of rebellion. Longwu General Li Jianyu, having escaped from the Tibetans and returned, was reported by his troops as communicating with the enemy—all were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 參悉治出之，人始屬望。

translations.literal: Can tried all cases and released them; people began to look to him with hope.
translations.idiomatic: Can tried all cases and released them. People began to look to him with hope.

sentences.zh: 俄以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事，領度支、鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Signatory Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat, concurrently serving as Commissioner of Revenue and Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed vice director of the Chancellery and co-signatory director of the Chancellery and Secretariat, concurrently serving as commissioner of revenue and salt and iron.

sentences.zh: 每延英對，它相罷，參必留，以度支為言，實專政也。

translations.literal: At each Yanying audience, when other chief ministers withdrew, Can always remained, speaking on revenue matters—in fact monopolizing governance.
translations.idiomatic: At each Yanying audience, when other chief ministers withdrew, Can always remained, speaking on revenue matters—in fact monopolizing governance.

sentences.zh: 然參無學術，不能稽古立事，惟樹親黨，多所诇察，四方畏之。

translations.literal: Yet Can had no learning; he could not consult antiquity to establish affairs, but only built factions of kinsmen and followers, spying extensively; all directions feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Can had no learning. He could not consult antiquity to establish affairs, but only built factions of kinsmen and followers, spying extensively. All directions feared him.

sentences.zh: 於是淄青李納厚饋參，外示嚴畏，實賂帝親近為間，故左右爭毀短之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ziqing's Li Na richly bribed Can, outwardly showing strict fear but in fact bribing the Emperor's intimates as spies; therefore those around the throne competed to slander him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Ziqing's Li Na richly bribed Can, outwardly showing strict fear but in fact bribing the emperor's intimates as spies. Therefore those around the throne competed to slander him.

sentences.zh: 申，其族子也，為給事中，參親愛，每除吏多訪申，申因得招賂，漏禁密語，故申所至，人目為「喜鵲」。

translations.literal: Shen was his clansman's son, serving as Supervising Censor; Can favored him; whenever appointing officials Can often consulted Shen; Shen thereby solicited bribes and leaked forbidden secrets; wherever Shen went, people called him the "Magpie."
translations.idiomatic: Shen was his clansman's son, serving as supervising censor. Can favored him. Whenever appointing officials Can often consulted Shen. Shen thereby solicited bribes and leaked forbidden secrets. Wherever Shen went, people called him the "Magpie."

sentences.zh: 帝聞，以戒參，且曰：「是必為累，不如斥之。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this, he admonished Can and said: "This will surely become a burden—it is better to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he admonished Can and said: "This will surely become a burden—it is better to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 參以情訴曰：「臣無強子姓，申雖疏屬，無它惡。」

translations.literal: Can pleaded emotionally: "Your subject has no powerful sons or clansmen; though Shen is a distant kinsman, he has no other evil."
translations.idiomatic: Can pleaded emotionally: "Your subject has no powerful sons or clansmen. Though Shen is a distant kinsman, he has no other evil."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「而雖自保，如外言何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Though you protect yourself, what of outside talk?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Though you protect yourself, what of outside talk?"

sentences.zh: 參固陳丐。

translations.literal: Can firmly petitioned and begged.
translations.idiomatic: Can firmly petitioned and begged.

sentences.zh: 初，陸贄與參不平，吳通玄兄弟皆在翰林，與贄軒輊不得，申舅嗣虢王則之與通微等善，遂共譖贄。

translations.literal: Initially, Lu Zhi and Can were at odds; the Wu Tongxuan brothers were all in the Hanlin Academy and could not compete with Zhi in rank; Shen's maternal uncle, Heir of Prince Guo Zezhi, was friendly with Tongwei and others, and together they slandered Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Lu Zhi and Can were at odds. The Wu Tongxuan brothers were all in the Hanlin Academy and could not compete with Zhi in rank. Shen's maternal uncle, Heir of Prince Guo Zezhi, was friendly with Tongwei and others, and together they slandered Zhi.

sentences.zh: 帝得其奸，逐申為道州司馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor learned of their treachery and exiled Shen as Military Staff Officer of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of their treachery and exiled Shen as military staff officer of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 不浹日，貶參郴州別駕。

translations.literal: Within less than a day, Can was demoted to Vice Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than a day, Can was demoted to vice prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣武劉士寧餉參絹五千，湖南觀察使李巽故與參隙，以狀聞，又中人為之驗左，帝大怒，以為外交戎臣，欲殺參。

translations.literal: Xuanwu's Liu Shining presented Can with five thousand bolts of silk; Hunan Regional Inspector Li Xun, formerly at odds with Can, reported this; palace envoys also verified it; the Emperor was greatly enraged, considering it illicit contact with frontier generals, and wished to kill Can.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu's Liu Shining presented Can with five thousand bolts of silk. Hunan regional inspector Li Xun, formerly at odds with Can, reported this. Palace envoys also verified it. The emperor was greatly enraged, considering it illicit contact with frontier generals, and wished to kill Can.

sentences.zh: 贄雖怨，然亦以殺之太重，乃貶州司馬，逐其息景伯於泉州，女尼於郴州，沒入貲產奴婢。

translations.literal: Though Zhi resented him, he also considered killing him too severe; Can was therefore demoted to military staff officer of the prefecture; his son Jingbo was exiled to Quanzhou, his daughter made a nun at Chenzhou, and property and slaves were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhi resented him, he also considered killing him too severe. Can was therefore demoted to military staff officer of the prefecture. His son Jingbo was exiled to Quanzhou, his daughter made a nun at Chenzhou, and property and slaves were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 帝又欲殺申、則之及屬人榮，贄固爭：「法有首從，首原則從減。

translations.literal: The Emperor also wished to kill Shen, Zezhi, and clansman Rong; Zhi firmly argued: "The law distinguishes principal and accomplice; when the principal is pardoned, the accomplice's penalty is reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wished to kill Shen, Zezhi, and clansman Rong. Zhi firmly argued: "The law distinguishes principal and accomplice. When the principal is pardoned, the accomplice's penalty is reduced.

sentences.zh: 榮與參雖善，然初無邪僻，數激憤有直言，晚頗疏忌，請貶榮遠官，申、則之除名流嶺南。」

translations.literal: Rong was friendly with Can, yet initially had no wickedness, often spoke bluntly in indignation, and in later years grew somewhat estranged and suspicious; I request demoting Rong to a distant post and exiling Shen and Zezhi to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was friendly with Can, yet initially had no wickedness, often spoke bluntly in indignation, and in later years grew somewhat estranged and suspicious. I request demoting Rong to a distant post and exiling Shen and Zezhi to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 時宦侍謗沮不已，參竟賜死於邕州，年六十。

translations.literal: At the time eunuch attendants slandered without cease; Can was ultimately granted death at Yongzhou, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: At the time eunuch attendants slandered without cease. Can was ultimately granted death at Yongzhou, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 而杖殺申，免榮死，諸竇並逐雲。

translations.literal: Shen was beaten to death; Rong was spared death; all the Dou clan were exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was beaten to death. Rong was spared death. All the Dou clan were exiled.

sentences.zh: 吳通玄者，海州人，與弟通微皆博學善文章。

translations.literal: Wu Tongxuan was a native of Hai Prefecture; he and his younger brother Tongwei were both broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tongxuan was a native of Hai Prefecture. He and his younger brother Tongwei were both broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 父道瓘，以道士詔授太子諸王經，故通玄等皆得侍太子遊，太子待之甚善。

translations.literal: Their father Daoguan, as a Daoist priest, was ordered by edict to teach the classics to the crown prince and princes; therefore Tongxuan and others all attended the crown prince in his travels, and the crown prince treated them very well.
translations.idiomatic: Their father Daoguan, as a Daoist priest, was ordered by edict to teach the classics to the crown prince and princes. Therefore Tongxuan and others all attended the crown prince in his travels, and the crown prince treated them very well.

sentences.zh: 始，通玄舉神童，補秘書正字。

translations.literal: Initially, Tongxuan passed the Precocious Talent examination and was appointed Corrector in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Tongxuan passed the Precocious Talent examination and was appointed corrector in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又擢文辭清麗科，調同州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He was also selected in the Elegant Literary Composition examination and was assigned as Military Staff Officer of the Household Registry in Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was also selected in the Elegant Literary Composition examination and was assigned as military staff officer of the household registry in Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，弟兄踵召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne, the brothers were successively summoned as Hanlin Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne, the brothers were successively summoned as Hanlin academicians.

sentences.zh: 頃之，通微遷職方郎中，通玄起居舍人，並知制誥。

translations.literal: Before long, Tongwei was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Appointments, and Tongxuan became Attendant of Daily Affairs; both drafted imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Tongwei was transferred to director in the Bureau of Appointments, and Tongxuan became attendant of daily affairs. Both drafted imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 凡帝有撰述，非通玄筆未嘗慊。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor had compositions to write, he was never satisfied unless Tongxuan's brush was used.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor had compositions to write, he was never satisfied unless Tongxuan's brush was used.

sentences.zh: 與陸贄、吉中孚、韋執誼並位。

translations.literal: He held rank alongside Lu Zhi, Ji Zhongfu, and Wei Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: He held rank alongside Lu Zhi, Ji Zhongfu, and Wei Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 贄文高有謀，特為帝器遇，且更險難，有功。

translations.literal: Zhi's writing was lofty and he was resourceful; he was especially valued by the Emperor, and had passed through danger and hardship with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's writing was lofty and he was resourceful. He was especially valued by the emperor and had passed through danger and hardship with merit.

sentences.zh: 通玄等特以東宮恩舊進，昵而不禮，見贄驟擢，頗冒恨。

translations.literal: Tongxuan and others had advanced solely through Eastern Palace favor as old associates; they were intimate yet disrespectful, and seeing Zhi's sudden promotion, they harbored considerable resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxuan and others had advanced solely through Eastern Palace favor as old associates. They were intimate yet disrespectful, and seeing Zhi's sudden promotion, they harbored considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 贄自恃勁正，屢短通玄於帝前，欲斥遠之，即建言：「承平時，工藝書畫之冗，皆待詔翰林而無學士，至德以來，命集賢學士入禁中草書詔，待進止於翰林院，因以名官。

translations.literal: Zhi, relying on his firm integrity, repeatedly spoke against Tongxuan before the Emperor, wishing to dismiss and distance him; he therefore proposed: "In times of peace, redundant artisans of craft, calligraphy, and painting were all Hanlin Attendants-in-Waiting without academicians; since Zhide, Imperial Library academicians were ordered into the inner palace to draft edicts, awaiting approval in the Hanlin Academy, and thus the office was named.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, relying on his firm integrity, repeatedly spoke against Tongxuan before the emperor, wishing to dismiss and distance him. He therefore proposed: "In times of peace, redundant artisans of craft, calligraphy, and painting were all Hanlin attendants-in-waiting without academicians. Since Zhide, Imperial Library academicians were ordered into the inner palace to draft edicts, awaiting approval in the Hanlin Academy, and thus the office was named.

sentences.zh: 今四方無事，制書職分宜歸中書舍人，請罷學士。」

translations.literal: Now the four directions are at peace; the duty of drafting edicts should return to secretariat draftsmen—I request abolishing the academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Now the four directions are at peace. The duty of drafting edicts should return to secretariat draftsmen—I request abolishing the academicians.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 通玄怨日結，謀奪其內職。

translations.literal: Tongxuan's resentment daily grew; he plotted to seize Zhi's inner-court duties.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxuan's resentment daily grew. He plotted to seize Zhi's inner-court duties.

sentences.zh: 會贄權知兵部侍郎，主貢舉，乃命為真。

translations.literal: When Zhi was acting Vice Minister of War and presided over the examinations, he was then appointed to the full post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi was acting vice minister of war and presided over the examinations, he was then appointed to the full post.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年，通玄拜諫議大夫，自以久次，當得中書舍人，大怨望。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan, Tongxuan was appointed Remonstrance Officer; considering his long seniority, he believed he should receive the post of Secretariat Draftsman, and was greatly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan, Tongxuan was appointed remonstrance officer. Considering his long seniority, he believed he should receive the post of secretariat draftsman, and was greatly resentful.

sentences.zh: 贄與竇參交惡，參從子申從舅嗣虢王則之方為金吾將軍，故申介之使結通玄兄弟，共危贄。

translations.literal: Zhi and Dou Can were mutually hostile; Can's clansman's son Shen and maternal uncle, Heir of Prince Guo Zezhi, were then General of the Imperial Guard; therefore Shen mediated to unite the Tongxuan brothers, jointly endangering Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Dou Can were mutually hostile. Can's clansman's son Shen and maternal uncle, Heir of Prince Guo Zezhi, were then general of the Imperial Guard. Therefore Shen mediated to unite the Tongxuan brothers, jointly endangering Zhi.

sentences.zh: 而通玄以宗室女為外婦，帝知，未及責。

translations.literal: Moreover, Tongxuan took an imperial clanswoman as a concubine outside marriage; the Emperor knew but had not yet reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Tongxuan took an imperial clanswoman as a concubine outside marriage. The emperor knew but had not yet reproached him.

sentences.zh: 則之飛謗云：「贄試進士，受賄謝。」
