translations.literal: Zezhi spread slander saying: "Zhi, in examining jinshi candidates, accepted bribes and gifts of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zezhi spread slander saying: "Zhi, in examining jinshi candidates, accepted bribes and gifts of thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝惡誣構，大怒，罷參宰相，逐則之昭州司馬，通玄泉州司馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor hated the false accusation, was greatly enraged, dismissed Can from the chief ministership, exiled Zezhi as Military Staff Officer of Zhaozhou and Tongxuan as Military Staff Officer of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated the false accusation and was greatly enraged. He dismissed Can from the chief ministership, exiled Zezhi as military staff officer of Zhaozhou and Tongxuan as military staff officer of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又銜淫汙近屬事，自詰之，不敢答，賜死長城驛。

translations.literal: Also bearing the matter of defiling a close kinswoman, the Emperor questioned him himself; Tongxuan dared not answer and was granted death at Changcheng Post.
translations.idiomatic: Also bearing the matter of defiling a close kinswoman, the emperor questioned him himself. Tongxuan dared not answer and was granted death at Changcheng Post.

sentences.zh: 贄遂相矣。

translations.literal: Zhi then became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi then became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 通玄死，通微白衣待罪於門，帝宥之，內懼禍，不敢行喪服。

translations.literal: When Tongxuan died, Tongwei waited in white robes at the gate to accept punishment; the Emperor pardoned him, but inwardly fearing disaster, he dared not wear mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongxuan died, Tongwei waited in white robes at the gate to accept punishment. The emperor pardoned him, but inwardly fearing disaster, he dared not wear mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：元載、楊炎各以才資奮，適主暗庸，故致位輔相。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Yuan Zai and Yang Yan each rose through talent and ability, meeting dim and mediocre rulers, and therefore reached the rank of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Yuan Zai and Yang Yan each rose through talent and ability, meeting dim and mediocre rulers, and therefore reached the rank of chief minister.

sentences.zh: 若其翦閹尹，城原州以謀西夏，還左藏有司，一租賦以檢制有亡，誠有取焉。

translations.literal: In cutting down eunuch power, fortifying Yuanzhou to plan against Western Xia, returning finances to the Left Treasury and responsible offices, and unifying rents and taxes to check surplus and deficit—these indeed had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In cutting down eunuch power, fortifying Yuanzhou to plan against Western Xia, returning finances to the Left Treasury and responsible offices, and unifying rents and taxes to check surplus and deficit—these indeed had merit.

sentences.zh: 然載本與輔國以利合，險刻著諸心，溪壑之欲，發乎無厭。

translations.literal: Yet Zai had originally allied with Fuguo for profit; cruelty and harshness were written in his heart; the desire of ravines and gullies sprang from insatiability.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zai had originally allied with Fuguo for profit. Cruelty and harshness were written in his heart. The desire of ravines and gullies sprang from insatiability.

sentences.zh: 炎牽連載勢，興醜裔，秉國維綱，返為載復讎，釋言於君，卒與妻子並誅，暴先骨，殛命於道，蓋自取之也。

translations.literal: Yan was implicated through Zai's power, rose from an ugly lineage, held the state's reins, yet in turn avenged Zai, spoke loosely to the ruler, and ultimately was executed together with wife and children, ancestral bones exposed, life ended on the road—this was largely self-inflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was implicated through Zai's power, rose from an ugly lineage, held the state's reins, yet in turn avenged Zai, spoke loosely to the ruler, and ultimately was executed together with wife and children, ancestral bones exposed, life ended on the road—this was largely self-inflicted.

sentences.zh: 夫奸人多才，未始不為患，故酆舒以俊死，而鄧析以辯亡。

translations.literal: Wicked men are often talented, and have never failed to bring calamity; therefore Feng Shu died for his handsomeness, and Deng Xi perished for his eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men are often talented, and have never failed to bring calamity. Therefore Feng Shu died for his handsomeness, and Deng Xi perished for his eloquence.

sentences.zh: 若兩人者，所謂多才者邪！

translations.literal: Are these two what is meant by the talented!
translations.idiomatic: Are these two what is meant by the talented!

sentences.zh: 縉言福業報應，參得君自私，無可論者。

translations.literal: Jin spoke of karmic merit and retribution; Can obtained the ruler through selfishness—there is nothing worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin spoke of karmic merit and retribution; Can obtained the ruler through selfishness—there is nothing worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱「鼎折足，其刑剭諒哉！

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "The cauldron's legs break—its punishment is mutilation—how credible!
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "The cauldron's legs break—its punishment is mutilation—how credible!
